description: Contradictory characterization of de-identification. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary', while participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method' and human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance states 'The public release is de-identified under the HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor method'. Removal of PHI plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications is an active de-identification action, which the 'NoDeIdentification' classification denies.
recommendation: Reconcile the de-identification classification with the stated Safe Harbor removal, e.g. record method as HIPAA Safe Harbor with a note that no direct identifiers were captured at source, rather than 'NoDeIdentification'.

description: The dedicated download_url slot is empty even though the dataset is publicly downloadable after self-attestation. The retrieval route is documented only in prose, inside data_governance.access_review_process ('The access route for version 3.0.0 is the FAIRhub access page at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access').
recommendation: Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access so machine clients can resolve the retrieval route without parsing governance prose.

description: No software is named in a data-producing or data-transforming role. The record describes format conversions in detail (Topcon .fda to DICOM, Heidelberg FLIO .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, Dexcom .csv to Open mHealth, ECG .xml to WFDB, REDCap to OMOP CDM tables) but never names the software that performed them, and no used_software attribute is populated on any preprocessing, cleaning, labeling or imputation entry. The software that is named falls in non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture tools, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure are hosting, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data. The GitHub organization link (https://github.com/AI-READI) is an account root that names no specific tool.
recommendation: Name and version the conversion and mapping software (e.g. the specific .fda/.sdt converters, the FIT-to-Open-mHealth mapper, the OMOP ETL implementation) on used_software of the relevant preprocessing_strategies entries, with repository links under the AI-READI GitHub organization.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', which no source states. The record's own source_caveats discloses that the RO-Crate gives 'HL7:2N (normal)' and FAIRhub gives accessType 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'. 'restricted' is the record's own mapping onto the schema enum, and a reader comparing to the upstream metadata will see a mismatch. The disclosure is exemplary; the residual risk is that the enum value overstates the access barrier for a publicly downloadable dataset.
recommendation: Retain the caveat but consider a less restrictive enum value consistent with self-attested public download, or add an explicit mapping table between the schema enum and the HL7/FAIRhub vocabularies.

description: Unresolved internal conflict on the size of the longitudinal follow-up arm: the FAIRhub healthsheet gives approximately 4% of participants while the FAIRhub README, the RO-Crate and NIH RePORTER give 10% of the cohort. Both figures are carried in collection_timeframes.source_caveats, relationships and known_limitations without resolution.
recommendation: Query the AI-READI team for the authoritative follow-up fraction and record a single value with the superseded figure noted.

description: The accountable institution is stated inconsistently across sources and is surfaced but not resolved: data_governance.accountable_organization and the license name Washington University in St. Louis (ROR 01yc7t268), while the RO-Crate places the principal investigator in the Department of Ophthalmology at the University of Washington, NIH RePORTER lists the University of Washington as awardee, and the IRB is the University of Washington IRB.
recommendation: Obtain a statement from the consortium on which institution is accountable for the released dataset as distinct from the awardee and the IRB of record.

description: sampling_strategies carries two mutually tensioned claims from the same tier 1 source: the healthsheet states the dataset 'contains all possible instances' and answers 'N/A' on sampling strategy, while the FAIRhub study description records the sampling method as 'Non-Probability Sample'. The record reconciles these in prose (the release is not a sample of enrollees, but enrollees are a non-probability sample of the study base), which is semantically correct, but the structured flags is_sample=true / is_representative=false only encode the second reading.
recommendation: Keep the prose reconciliation and consider splitting the flags by level (release vs enrolled cohort vs study base).

description: No data_protection_impacts entry and no future_use_impacts entry exist. The absence of a DPIA is disclosed in notes ('no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'), and anticipated downstream social impact is addressed only indirectly through bias mitigation and the stated motivation for withholding race/ethnicity to prevent stigmatization.
recommendation: Add a future_use_impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) entry capturing the anticipated downstream social impacts of AI models trained on the release, and consider a DPIA now that a re-identification risk is acknowledged.

description: data_governance names a committee (AI-READI Consortium) and an accountable organization but records no committee contact person or address. A general project contact (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact) and the IRB reliance mailbox (hsdrely@uw.edu) appear elsewhere, so a reader can reach someone, but not the governance body specifically.
recommendation: Populate data_governance.committee_contact with the named contact for the body that adjudicates controlled-access requests.

description: Variable metadata is rich in units, measurement technique and reference ranges but carries no external variable identifiers (LOINC, SNOMED, OMOP concept ids) despite the clinical tables being mapped one-to-one onto the OMOP Common Data Model, where such concept ids exist.
recommendation: Attach OMOP concept ids or LOINC codes to the laboratory and vital-sign variables to make the variable layer machine-linkable to other OMOP datasets.

description: The deidentification characterization is internally contradictory. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary', while participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that PHI 'was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method' and is_deidentified.identifiers_removed lists PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications as removed and held under controlled access. Removal via Safe Harbor and 'no de-identification was necessary because no identifiers were collected' cannot both describe the same release.
recommendation: State one controlling account: either the source-system fields never captured HIPAA identifiers (in which case Safe Harbor was a verification step, not a removal step), or identifiers were captured and removed under Safe Harbor. The record already contains both statements verbatim from different upstream sources; add a source_caveats note on is_deidentified resolving or explicitly flagging the conflict, as the record does elsewhere.

description: No software is named for the pipeline that produced the distributed files. preprocessing_strategies describes .fda to DICOM, .sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth, .xml to WFDB conversions and OMOP CDM mapping, and characterizes version 2.0.0/3.0.0 processing as 'a combination of automated and custom processing', but no converter, mapper or pipeline is named. The named software in the record occupies non-producing roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are data capture (role a), FAIRhub is hosting (role b), and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard validates the released tables (role d). The GitHub organization link is an account root identifying the publisher, not a named tool.
recommendation: Name the conversion and mapping software with versions (for example the .fda/.sdt to DICOM converters, the FIT to Open mHealth mapper, the xml to WFDB tool, and the OMOP ETL) and attach them via used_software on the relevant preprocessing_strategies entries, with links to the specific AI-READI repositories rather than the organization root.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is recorded as 'restricted', a value the record itself states no source asserts: the RO-Crate gives 'HL7:2N (normal)' and FAIRhub gives accessType 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'. 'restricted' overstates the barrier relative to a publicly downloadable release gated only by identity verification, a use attestation and licence acceptance.
recommendation: Retain the transparent source_caveats note but consider the enum value that best matches self-attested public download, and record the HL7 confidentiality code alongside the enum so the mapping is recoverable.

description: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk assesses a theoretical future re-identification risk driven by AI inference over multimodal data, yet notes records that no data protection impact analysis has been conducted and there is no data_protection_impacts block. HIPAA Safe Harbor addresses tabular identifiers and does not speak to the re-identification surface of high-dimensional retinal DICOM, ten-day CGM traces and wearable activity streams, which are the bulk of the 3.82 TB release.
recommendation: Add a data_protection_impacts entry covering the imaging and sensor modalities specifically, or state why a DPIA was judged unnecessary; is_deidentified.deidentification_details currently leaves the healthsheet's blank answer about post-deidentification re-identification measures unfilled.

description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated. The access route (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access) and the three-step access procedure appear only in data_governance.access_review_process prose, and the landing page appears in page.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint so machine clients can resolve the retrieval route without parsing governance prose.

description: data_governance.committee_contact is absent. A governance committee is named (AI-READI Consortium) and an accountable organization given, but the only contact addresses in the record are maintainers (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact) and the IRB reliance team (hsdrely@uw.edu), neither of which is presented as the governance committee contact.
recommendation: Add data_governance.committee_contact, particularly for the Data Access Committee that the protocol says governs the controlled-access tier.

description: No future_use_impacts block exists. Anticipated downstream social impact reasoning is present but distributed: removal of race and sex 'to prevent stigmatization of findings', the recommended splits 'aimed at reducing disparities in models developed using the dataset', watermarking and licence terms to deter re-identification, and the Community Advisory Board review. Conflicts of interest are not addressed anywhere.
recommendation: Consolidate the dispersed social-impact reasoning into future_use_impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) and add a conflict-of-interest statement to ethical_reviews.

description: Three substantive source conflicts remain unresolved rather than adjudicated: the accountable institution (Washington University in St. Louis per FAIRhub and the licence, versus University of Washington per the RO-Crate, the IRB and NIH RePORTER), the longitudinal follow-up arm (approximately 4% per the healthsheet versus 10% per the README, RO-Crate and RePORTER), and the sampling characterization ('contains all possible instances' versus 'Non-Probability Sample' within the same FAIRhub record). The record discloses each conflict explicitly in source_caveats, which is good documentation practice, but a reuser cannot determine the correct value.
recommendation: Where tier ranking does not settle a conflict, seek an authoritative statement from the AI-READI team and record the resolution; retain the caveat trail for provenance.

description: Two incompatible accounts of the same de-identification process. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' with the explanation that 'no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary', while participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that 'Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method'. Removal via Safe Harbor and 'no identifiers were collected, so no de-identification was necessary' cannot both describe the same release. is_deidentified.identifiers_removed then lists specific removed elements (PHI, sex, race/ethnicity, medications), which supports the removal account and contradicts the 'NoDeIdentification' label.
recommendation: Reconcile the two statements in one place: either record the method as HIPAA Safe Harbor with the 'NoDeIdentification' source label noted as the upstream record's classification, or state explicitly that the upstream type field is a registry artifact and that Safe Harbor review was in fact performed.

description: Element 8 sub-element 4 is unmet. Every released modality passed through a format transformation (.fda and .sdt converted to DICOM, .FIT converted to Open mHealth, .csv mapped to Open mHealth, .xml mapped to WFDB, REDCap exports mapped one-to-one onto OMOP CDM tables), and the processing regime is characterised only as 'custom and ad hoc handling for version 1.0.0' moving to 'a combination of automated and custom processing' for versions 2.0.0 and 3.0.0. No used_software is attached to preprocessing_strategies or cleaning_strategies and no converter, mapper or pipeline is named. The software that is named occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture instruments, FAIRhub is the hosting platform, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is a validation tool run against the released tables. The GitHub organisation link is an account root that identifies the publisher rather than naming a piece of software.
recommendation: Attach used_software to the preprocessing_strategies entries naming the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converters, the .FIT-to-Open-mHealth converter, the ECG-XML-to-WFDB mapper and the REDCap-to-OMOP ETL, each with a version and, where published, the specific repository under github.com/AI-READI rather than the organisation root.

description: No download_url field is populated. The access route is recoverable only from data_governance.access_review_process prose, which names https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and the three access steps (verified-ID login, T2DM-research use attestation, license acceptance). The information is actionable but is not in the slot a harvester would read.
recommendation: Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, retaining the prose description of the self-attestation steps.

description: data_governance.committee_contact is not populated. The governance committee is named ('AI-READI Consortium') and an accountable organization with a ROR is given, but no contact person or address is attached to the governance role. Contacts do appear elsewhere in the record (contact@aireadi.org via maintainers, hsdrely@uw.edu as the IRB reliance contact), so a reader can reach someone, but not the governance committee as such.
recommendation: Add data_governance.committee_contact, pointing either to contact@aireadi.org or to the Data Access Committee address once that body's requirements are finalised.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', which the record's own source_caveats identify as its mapping rather than a source value: the RO-Crate gives 'HL7:2N (normal)' and the FAIRhub dataset description gives accessType 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired'. 'Restricted' is a defensible reading of self-attestation plus a restrictive license, but it is more severe than 'normal' and a consumer filtering on the enum will classify this public release alongside genuinely controlled data. The disclosure of the mapping is itself good practice and is why this is scored low rather than as a correctness failure.
recommendation: Keep the caveat and consider recording the verbatim source values ('HL7:2N (normal)', 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired') in an adjacent field so the enum mapping is machine-traceable, not only readable in prose.

description: Unresolved source disagreements are carried rather than silently merged, but they do leave three facts indeterminate for a reader: the longitudinal follow-up arm is given as approximately 4% (FAIRhub healthsheet) and as 10% (FAIRhub README, RO-Crate, NIH RePORTER); the accountable institution is Washington University in St. Louis (FAIRhub, license Licensor) or the University of Washington (RO-Crate, NIH RePORTER awardee, IRB location); and enrolment start is 18 July 2023 (BMJ Open) or 19 July 2023 (FAIRhub). All three conflicts are between or within tier 1 sources, so the record's own ranking rule does not settle them.
recommendation: Retain the dual reporting, which is the correct handling, and where possible add a provenance note recording which value the AI-READI team confirms, so downstream consumers do not have to re-adjudicate.

description: No data_protection_impacts and no future_use_impacts blocks. The record states explicitly in notes that 'no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted', which is honest negative documentation rather than an omission, but it means the re-identification risk assessment in participant_privacy stands without a formal DPIA behind it, and anticipated downstream social impacts are addressed only obliquely (stigmatization-motivated withholding of sex and race/ethnicity, community advisory board review).
recommendation: Record a short DPIA or a structured future_use_impacts entry covering the AI re-identification risk the record already names as its motivation for watermarking and the licence regime.

description: Institutional attribution is internally discordant. The principal investigator Aaron Y. Lee is given the affiliation 'Washington University in St. Louis' with ROR:01yc7t268, and data_governance.accountable_organization repeats it, while every operational fact in the record points to the University of Washington: the IRB is University of Washington protocol STUDY00016228 with a uw.edu reliance contact and a Seattle postal address, NIH RePORTER records the awardee organization as University of Washington, the LeeLab Anura sensor was built at the University of Washington Karalis Johnson Retina Center, and central laboratory assays ran at the University of Washington Nutrition and Obesity Research Center. The record discloses the conflict in three source_caveats and resolves it by source tier rather than by plausibility, so the asserted accountable organization is likely an upstream FAIRhub conflation of two distinct institutions carried into the datasheet.
recommendation: Retain the tier-1 value but annotate the ROR as contested, or reconcile with the awardee organization in NIH RePORTER; at minimum avoid attaching ROR:01yc7t268 to a principal investigator whom the same record situates in the University of Washington Department of Ophthalmology.

description: No software is named for any step that produced or transformed the distributed data. The release passed through substantial conversion — Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt to DICOM, Philips XML to WFDB, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, REDCap exports to OMOP CDM tables, environmental readings to the NASA ASCII Earth-science format, plus static watermarking — and none of the seven preprocessing_strategies or three cleaning_strategies carries a used_software attachment or names a converter, pipeline or library. The software that is named occupies other roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application capture data, FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure hosts it, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard validates it. external_resources points at the GitHub organisation root https://github.com/AI-READI, which identifies the publisher rather than naming a tool.
recommendation: Attach used_software to each preprocessing and cleaning strategy naming the converter and version (for example the .fda and .sdt to DICOM converters and the OMOP ETL), and link the specific AI-READI repositories rather than the organisation root.

description: The deidentification account holds two readings in tension. FAIRhub records deIdentType 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentDirect true and deIdentHIPAA true, explaining that no identifiers were collected so none was necessary, while the Nature Metabolism comment describes the public set as stripped of PHI via the HIPAA Safe Harbor method — an active procedure. The record also notes that the healthsheet question on measures taken to avoid re-identification was left unanswered. The tension is explicitly surfaced in is_deidentified.source_caveats and the two readings agree on the outcome (no PHI in the public release), which substantially mitigates it.
recommendation: Ask the project to state whether a Safe Harbor determination was performed on the imaging and wearable streams, which is not answered by 'no identifiers were collected' for DICOM headers.

description: No top-level download_url is populated. Platform access is nonetheless locatable: every distribution_formats entry carries access_urls https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.access_review_process states the three access steps.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint so that harvesters reading the dedicated slot find it.

description: Character encoding is not stated for any distribution. Formats are otherwise fully specified with media types, and the omission matters little for the binary DICOM, WFDB and .FIT-derived streams, but the CSV, TSV, JSON and Markdown members leave encoding unstated.
recommendation: Declare UTF-8 (or the actual encoding) on the text-based distribution entries.

description: No governance committee contact person is asserted. data_governance.source_caveats states plainly that no source designates one; a committee_name (AI-READI Consortium) and general contacts (contact@aireadi.org, https://aireadi.org/contact, https://docs.aireadi.org/docs/3/contact) are given instead, and the Data Access Committee referenced for the controlled set is unnamed.
recommendation: Name a contact for the Data Access Committee, which requesters of the controlled-access set need in order to initiate the institutional agreement.

description: The variables block documents 26 representative measures in depth but carries no per-variable ontology or concept identifiers. Coded vocabularies are referenced only at the collection level (OMOP CDM one-to-one table mapping, RxNorm for medications), so a variable such as hba1c has no LOINC or OMOP concept ID attached, and the block covers a fraction of the full OMOP variable inventory.
recommendation: Attach LOINC or OMOP concept identifiers to the clinical and laboratory variables and state that the block is a representative selection over the full OMOP inventory.

description: Version 2.0.0 is recorded in version_access.version_details as no longer accessible, yet it is listed among versions_available with its DOI and appears in related_datasets as an is_new_version_of target. The claim is accurate rather than wrong, but a consumer resolving doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 from the relationship will not retrieve data.
recommendation: Mark the 2.0.0 entry as withdrawn where it is listed as a relationship target, not only in the prose version_details.

description: data_protection_impacts records that no data protection impact analysis was conducted. This is a documented absence rather than a silent one, and a formal DPIA is not required of a US NIH study, but it leaves the element-4 assessment resting entirely on the IRB record.
recommendation: Given the acknowledged AI-driven re-identification risk, consider a documented risk assessment even where no regulatory DPIA is required.

description: No software is named for the transformations that produced the distributed data. preprocessing_strategies states in the passive voice that 'Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt files are converted to DICOM, Garmin .FIT files are converted to the Open mHealth standard, and electrocardiogram data are stored in the WaveForm DataBase (WFDB) format', but names no converter, pipeline or version. Every tool the record does name occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure are hosting, the RO-Crate/FAIRscape profile is metadata production, and the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data rather than its production. The GitHub pointer identifies only the publisher organisation.
recommendation: Name the conversion software and versions used for .fda/.sdt to DICOM, .FIT to Open mHealth and WFDB encoding, and link the specific AI-READI repositories that implement them rather than the organisation root.

description: is_deidentified.method simultaneously reports that the FAIRhub dataset description records the de-identification type as 'NoDeIdentification' and that the public set is stripped of PHI 'using the Safe Harbor method', with identifiers_removed listing HIPAA PHI plus sex, race/ethnicity and medications. The two statements describe the same release and pull in opposite directions; the record flags the tension but leaves the structured method value carrying both readings.
recommendation: State the operative determination (HIPAA Safe Harbor applied, plus removal of sex, race/ethnicity and medications) as the structured method, and relegate the FAIRhub 'NoDeIdentification' registry label to notes with an explanation of why the registry flag differs.

description: variables is an explicitly partial inventory: eight substantive entries plus a 'Representative subset marker' entry stating that the complete variable documentation lives at https://docs.aireadi.org. No per-variable persistent identifiers (OMOP concept IDs, LOINC codes, column names) are given for any entry, so variable-level cross-dataset linking must be resolved outside the datasheet.
recommendation: Add OMOP concept IDs or LOINC codes to the listed variables and state the count of the full inventory, so the partial list is bounded and machine-linkable.

description: total_size_bytes (3,815,969,779,678) exceeds the sum of the nine datatype directory sizes (3,815,969,360,064) by 419,614 bytes. The record discloses the gap in source_caveats item (7) and states that the bundle does not explain it. The parallel file-count gap (356,343 total vs 356,334 across directories) is fully reconciled by the nine root-level metadata files, so only the byte discrepancy is unresolved.
recommendation: Recompute the directory byte totals against the release manifest and either correct the figure or state what the 419,614 bytes comprise.

description: Responsible-organisation conflict left unreconciled: data_governance.accountable_organization is Washington University in St. Louis (ROR:01yc7t268) and the licence names it as Licensor, while ethical_reviews and human_subject_research place IRB oversight, the reviewing body address and the reliance contact at the University of Washington. The RO-Crate label 'Washington University IRB' with a uw.edu contact compounds the ambiguity. The record discloses all of this in source_caveats items (2) and (3).
recommendation: Obtain a single authoritative statement of the sponsoring institution and the reviewing IRB, and record the other institution explicitly as a reliance site rather than leaving two tier-1 readings side by side.

description: The planned longitudinal follow-up fraction is given as both 10% of the cohort (NIH RePORTER and the FAIRhub study description) and approximately 4% (healthsheet). The record records both rather than selecting, and correctly omits the figure from collection_timeframes rather than asserting one.
recommendation: Resolve against the current protocol amendment and record the superseded figure with its date.

description: Two related_datasets entries use relationship_type 'is_described_by' with target_dataset pointing at journal-article DOIs (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x, 10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449) rather than datasets. The record itself flags that these targets are articles, so the slot is being used deliberately to carry an attested relationship the schema has no better home for.
recommendation: Move article references to a publication or citation slot if one becomes available, retaining the typed relationship for genuine dataset targets.

description: Two governance values are derived by the datasheet author rather than quoted from a source: confidentiality_level 'restricted' is inferred from the access model (the RO-Crate's own term is 'HL7:2N (normal)'), and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' is inferred from statements that no identifiers were collected and Safe Harbor was applied, with no source making a compliance determination in those words. Both derivations are disclosed in regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats and are reasonable, but they are judgements rather than attested facts.
recommendation: Retain the derivation disclosure and, if possible, cite a source that makes the compliance determination explicitly.

description: No dedicated governance committee contact is recorded. data_governance carries committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact; the reachable addresses are the study central contact (contact@aireadi.org) under maintainers and the IRB reliance mailbox (hsdrely@uw.edu) under human_subject_research. A prospective user with a governance question has no named committee contact.
recommendation: Add data_governance.committee_contact naming the Data Access Committee contact for controlled-access enquiries.

description: No imputation_protocols slot is present. The substance is covered elsewhere: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states that missing values were filled only where directly derivable from other portions of an individual's record, under site PI approval, and otherwise left missing, with no instances excluded. This documents that statistical imputation was not used, but it is not discoverable from the imputation slot.
recommendation: Add an imputation_protocols entry recording explicitly that no statistical imputation was performed, cross-referencing the handling strategy.

description: sensitive_elements_present: false and confidential_elements_present: false sit uneasily with regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level: restricted, HIPAA-oriented handling, static watermarking of released copies, verified-ID access gating and an acknowledged theoretical re-identification risk. A release that genuinely contains nothing sensitive or confidential would not normally require that control stack; the two blocks appear to answer the healthsheet's narrow questions rather than characterise the release as governed.
recommendation: Qualify sensitive_elements/confidential_elements to state that the released variables are not themselves sensitive while the release remains access-controlled because of residual re-identification risk, so the two claims are read together rather than as a contradiction.

description: is_deidentified carries three mutually inconsistent source statements: FAIRhub records 'NoDeIdentification' (no identifiers collected), the RO-Crate records the release as deidentified, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping. The structured method field asserts the strongest of the three (HIPAA Safe Harbor) while deidentification_details reports all three unreconciled.
recommendation: State which statement the project treats as authoritative for the released files, or record the method as 'Safe Harbor verification, no identifiers collected' so the structured value and the prose do not diverge.

description: No download_url field is populated. The download route is nevertheless reconstructable from page, data_governance.access_review_process (verified-ID login, T2DM-only attestation, license assent) and the external resource https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access, so the sub-element's purpose is met by platform access instructions rather than by a direct link.
recommendation: Populate download_url with https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 or the access endpoint so machine clients can resolve the retrieval route without parsing prose.

description: distribution_formats lists DICOM, CSV, JSON and Markdown, but the release also distributes WFDB electrocardiography records, Open mHealth wearable/CGM payloads and NASA ESDS-style ASCII environmental files per conforms_to and file_collections. The distribution list is narrower than the standards list, and no character encoding is stated anywhere.
recommendation: Add distribution_formats entries for WFDB and the Open mHealth/ESDS text payloads with their media types, and record character encoding (e.g. UTF-8) for the text-based collections.

description: is_tabular: false while the description states the modalities 'encompass tabular data, imaging data and physiological signal/waveform data' and clinical_data is distributed as one-to-one OMOP CDM CSV tables. The flag is defensible for a multimodal release that is not a single table, but read alone it contradicts the description.
recommendation: Note beside is_tabular that the release is multimodal and that tabular content is confined to the OMOP clinical_data collection and participants.tsv.

description: No software that produced or transformed the released data is named. Conversion of Topcon .fda and FLIO .sdt exports to DICOM, of Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, and mapping of clinical data to OMOP CDM are described as having happened, but no tool, package, version or repository is attached to any of those steps, and no used_software is recorded on preprocessing_strategies or cleaning_strategies. The software that is named occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture instrumentation; FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting; the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation of the released data; https://github.com/AI-READI is an organisation root that identifies the publisher rather than a piece of software.
recommendation: Name the converters and mapping pipelines (tool name, version, and the AI-READI repository that holds each) on preprocessing_strategies.used_software so a reader can tell what produced the distributed DICOM, OMOP and Open mHealth files.

description: variables provides 20 measures with name, data type, unit, description and measurement technique, but no ontology or concept identifiers (LOINC, OMOP concept_id, SNOMED) are attached, and source_caveats records that the authoritative per-domain data dictionary at docs.aireadi.org was not consulted. Variable coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive for a 356,343-file multimodal release.
recommendation: Attach concept identifiers to each variable and link the released participants.json / per-domain data dictionary as the authoritative variable reference.

description: No errata block and no data_protection_impacts (DPIA) block. Change information is instead carried by updates.update_details and version_access.version_details, and data-protection reasoning by participant_privacy and ethical_reviews, so both sub-elements are satisfied through their alternative fields rather than left undocumented.
recommendation: Add an errata list (empty with a statement if none are known) and a short DPIA record referencing the re-identification analysis already present in future_use_impacts.

description: Institutional attribution is internally contradictory across the record: Washington University in St. Louis is named as licensor, accountable organization and PI affiliation, while the reviewing IRB, the award recipient per NIH RePORTER and the assay laboratory are all University of Washington. The record discloses the conflict in source_caveats rather than resolving it, which is honest but leaves accountable_organization pointing at an institution that no human-subjects or award evidence supports.
recommendation: Resolve the attribution with the project, or mark accountable_organization as reported-by-FAIRhub and name the University of Washington as the human-subjects and award institution.

description: Collection start is given as 2023-07-19 in collection_timeframes and the description while the BMJ Open protocol states 18 July 2023; license naming differs between two tier-1 sources ('AI-READI custom license v2.0' in the API, 'Health Data License' on the dataset page); a healthsheet answer describing first-year coverage contradicts the stated 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01 window. All three are disclosed and adjudicated by source tier rather than left silent.
recommendation: Retain the tier adjudication; where the project can confirm a single value upstream, cite the confirmation so downstream consumers stop inheriting the ambiguity.

description: No software that produced or transformed the distributed data is named. preprocessing_strategies states that Topcon .fda and Heidelberg .sdt exports were 'converted to DICOM', Garmin .FIT 'converted to the Open mHealth standard', ECG 'converted to WFDB', and that clinical data were 'mapped to' the OMOP CDM, but no converter, mapper or pipeline is identified; processing is described only as 'a combination of automated and custom processing'. The named software in the record occupies non-qualifying roles: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture, FAIRhub on Microsoft Azure is hosting, the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard is validation, and https://github.com/AI-READI is an organization root that identifies the publisher rather than a tool.
recommendation: Name the conversion and OMOP-mapping software with versions and repository or DOI links (for example the specific .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converters and the FIT-to-Open-mHealth tooling), attaching them via used_software on preprocessing_strategies.

description: No download_url slot is populated even though the release is publicly downloadable. Access is nevertheless actionable from other slots: distribution_formats.access_urls gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access and data_governance.access_review_process records the FAIRhub access type 'PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired' and the three steps required.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub download endpoint so that machine agents need not infer it from distribution_formats.

description: The de-identification evidence carries an internal tension the record itself surfaces: is_deidentified.deidentification_details reports the FAIRhub deIdentType as 'NoDeIdentification' with deIdentHIPAA true, while is_deidentified.method asserts the public set is stripped of PHI 'via the Safe Harbor method'. The record reconciles this by explaining that no identifiers were collected so no active de-identification step was necessary, which is a coherent reading, but the two statements read as contradictory in isolation.
recommendation: State explicitly that 'NoDeIdentification' denotes the absence of a removal step on an already identifier-free collection, rather than the absence of HIPAA conformance.

description: total_size_bytes is stated as 3,815,969,779,678 while the nine file_collections directory sizes sum to 3,815,969,360,064, a difference of 419,614 bytes that no source accounts for. The record discloses this discrepancy in source_caveats and attributes it plausibly to the root-level metadata files.
recommendation: Publish a byte count for the root metadata directory so that the stated total reconciles with the per-directory sums.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted' and hipaa_compliant 'compliant' are the record's own mappings onto the schema vocabulary, not values any source states; the only source value is the RO-Crate's 'HL7:2N (normal)'. The record declares this inference in source_caveats rather than presenting the enum values as sourced, which is the correct handling, but a consumer reading only the structured slot would not see the inference.
recommendation: Carry the source value 'HL7:2N (normal)' in a notes field adjacent to the enum so the mapping is visible at the point of use.

description: variables documents 13 variables (participant_id, seven laboratory analytes, MoCA, visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, CGM, particulate matter) for a release whose clinical_data directory is a one-to-one mapping of OMOP CDM tables covering surveys, assessments and laboratory results. Variable-level coverage is therefore illustrative rather than exhaustive, though the entries present carry data_type, unit, measurement_technique, reference ranges and an is_identifier flag.
recommendation: Reference participants.json and the OMOP CDM table definitions as the authoritative data dictionary, or state explicitly that the variables list is a curated subset.

description: data_governance records committee_name, accountable_organization, access_review_process and stewardship_roles but no committee_contact. A contact is reachable elsewhere (maintainers gives contact@aireadi.org and https://aireadi.org/contact; human_subject_research.ethics_review_board gives hsdrely@uw.edu for the IRB Reliance Team), so the governance-contact requirement is met in substance but not in the dedicated slot.
recommendation: Populate data_governance.committee_contact with the Data Access Committee or consortium governance contact.

description: Three named evidence slots are empty where their subject matter is nevertheless addressed in prose: errata (change information is instead in updates.update_details and version_access.version_details), imputation_protocols (missing-value handling is in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy), and data_protection_impacts (the notes field states that no data protection impact analysis has been conducted).
recommendation: Populate the dedicated slots, including an explicit negative for data_protection_impacts, so the negative findings currently buried in notes become machine-readable.

description: Element 8 sub-element 4: the record describes format conversion and processing of the released data (.fda and .sdt to DICOM, Garmin .FIT to Open mHealth, 'a combination of automated and custom processing') but never names the software that performed any of it. Every piece of software named in the record occupies an excluded role: REDCap and the MoCA Duo application are capture and data-entry tools (role a); FAIRhub is the hosting and dissemination platform (role b); the RO-Crate packaging wraps the release without transforming its contents (role c); the OMOP CDM Data Quality Dashboard, supported by the included dqd_omop.json, is a validation aid for downstream users (role d). The GitHub pointer is an organization root (https://github.com/AI-READI) that identifies the publisher rather than a named conversion or processing tool.
recommendation: Name the conversion and processing software with versions (for example the .fda/.sdt-to-DICOM converters, the Garmin .FIT-to-mHealth converter and the OMOP ETL tooling) and link the specific repositories under the AI-READI GitHub organization rather than the organization root.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is set to 'restricted', a value the record itself states is its own substitution that 'does not reproduce, and on its face contradicts' the only sourced classification, the RO-Crate's HL7:2N (normal). It also sits against confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present: false. The substitution is disclosed rather than concealed, which is good practice, but the asserted enum value is not supported by any source.
recommendation: Either carry the sourced HL7:2N value in a notes-bearing slot and leave the enum unset, or add an explicit crosswalk justifying the mapping from HL7:2N to 'restricted' on the basis of the access gating rather than the sensitivity classification.

description: Three incompatible characterizations of deidentification are carried simultaneously: is_deidentified.method reports FAIRhub's 'NoDeIdentification' with identifiable_elements_present: false (no identifiers collected into the release), the RO-Crate records deidentified: true, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping of Protected Health Information. Safe Harbor stripping and 'no de-identification was necessary' are different operational claims about the same release. The record documents the disagreement in source_caveats rather than resolving it.
recommendation: State which operation was actually performed on the released files (a Safe Harbor review versus a confirmation that no identifiers were ever routed into the release) and demote the other characterizations to provenance notes.

description: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present is true, enumerating EHR, wearable, ECG, environmental and CGM categories from the RO-Crate, while the FAIRhub healthsheet position recorded in the same block asserts the public dataset contains no sensitive data, and confidential_elements_present is false. Both tier-1 positions are retained without adjudication.
recommendation: Adjudicate on the released files specifically: the categories the RO-Crate lists are all present in the public release, which favours the affirmative flag with the healthsheet answer scoped to direct identifiers.

description: sampling_strategies.is_sample is false while the same block documents non-probability, wave-based stratified recruitment from an EHR-derived study base with deliberate under- and oversampling. The record scopes is_sample to enrollment completeness and warns the reader, but the boolean read alone contradicts the prose.
recommendation: Set is_sample true with respect to the target population and keep the enrollment-completeness claim in prose, or add an explicit scope qualifier to the boolean.

description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is nonetheless fully actionable: page gives https://fairhub.io/datasets/3 and data_governance.access_review_process publishes the access route at https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access together with the exact conditions (verified ID login, type-2-diabetes-research attestation, license acceptance, access type PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired).
recommendation: Populate download_url with the FAIRhub access endpoint so machine clients do not have to parse the governance prose.

description: No errata slot is populated. Change documentation is carried by updates.update_details pointing at the CHANGELOG, by the version_access note that 2.0.0 is no longer accessible, and by the known_limitations entry recording that Snellen visual acuity variables were dropped in 3.0.0; no corrections to previously released values are reported as such.
recommendation: Add an errata list, or state explicitly that no corrections to previously released data have been issued, so the silence is distinguishable from an omission.

description: instances.data_topic carries the bare CURIE B2AI_TOPIC:43 with no label or resolvable URI, so the coded topic is not machine- or human-resolvable from the record alone. The condition coverage is recoverable from description, subpopulations and known_limitations (type 2 diabetes across four severity arms), which is why the sub-element still passes.
recommendation: Add the human-readable label and a resolvable prefix expansion for the B2AI_TOPIC CURIE.

description: Unresolved institutional attribution: the acronym expansion ('Exploratory' versus 'Equitable'), the lead institution (Washington University in St. Louis as FAIRhub managing organization and license Licensor versus University of Washington as RO-Crate PI affiliation and NIH RePORTER awardee) and the publisher (FAIRhub versus AI-READI Consortium) each differ between equally ranked sources. The record carries both positions in source_caveats rather than asserting one silently, which is the correct handling, but a consumer of creators.principal_investigator.affiliation receives two affiliations for one person.
recommendation: Distinguish the roles explicitly: administering/sponsoring institution versus the PI's academic department, which would let both values stand without conflict.

description: The RO-Crate copyright notice quoted in ip_restrictions reads 'Copyright (c) 2026 AI-READI' for a release issued 2025-11-17. The value is faithfully quoted from the source, so this is a source artifact rather than a record error, but it is temporally inconsistent with issued and distribution_dates.
recommendation: Note the discrepancy against the source rather than leaving the future-dated notice unremarked.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true for a 50,000-admission multicenter retrospective clinical dataset, but no IRB, ethics committee, approval identifier, or waiver determination is recorded anywhere. The two ethical_reviews entries describe consortium ethics activity (community focus groups, an 'Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' pillar, legal-landscape analysis) and their own source_caveats concede that 'the bundle names no IRB, ethics committee, or approval identifier, and does not state that any body performed a formal ethical review of the dataset.'
recommendation: Record the reviewing IRB(s) for the coordinating centre and contributing sites with approval or exemption/waiver identifiers, or state explicitly that the extraction proceeded under a documented waiver of consent and name the body that granted it.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true but the informed_consent field is entirely absent. For retrospective EHR extraction a waiver of consent is the expected documentation, and neither consent nor waiver is stated.
recommendation: Add informed_consent describing the consent basis (waiver of informed consent under 45 CFR 46.116, broad consent, or opt-out), the granting body, and any withdrawal mechanism.

description: human_subject_research.special_populations identifies pediatric (PICU) and neonatal (NICU) intensive care patients — classic vulnerable populations — yet at_risk_populations and participant_compensation are both absent, so no protections specific to minors are documented.
recommendation: Populate at_risk_populations with the additional safeguards applied to pediatric and neonatal records (parental permission basis, age-shifting or date-jitter, access restrictions) and state explicitly that compensation is not applicable to retrospective extraction.

description: status is 'partially released' and updates.update_details describes an actively expanding release (50,000 of an anticipated 100,000 admissions, imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process), yet no version, version_access, or errata are recorded. A user cannot name or re-obtain the snapshot they analysed.
recommendation: Assign a version identifier to each enclave snapshot, document how prior versions are reached, and maintain a dated change log.

description: known_limitations documents pronounced and uneven modality availability (1000 images with de-identification in process, EEG extraction in process, note tokens only), which is a documented missingness pattern, but missing_data_documentation and anomalies are both absent and no imputation_protocols statement is given.
recommendation: Add missing_data_documentation quantifying per-modality coverage per admission, and either document imputation protocols or state that no imputation is performed.

description: purposes state the goal of developing 'a publicly available, AI-ready critical care dataset', while description, license_and_use_terms and confidential_elements state that all nine modalities are under controlled access conditional on a signed licensing agreement, with one route additionally requiring a '.edu' address. The aspiration and the realised access regime are not reconciled.
recommendation: Distinguish the programmatic aspiration from the current access regime, and state whether any modality or derived summary is intended for open release.

description: regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is absent although the dataset is derived from US hospital protected health information, and is_deidentified carries no named standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor / Expert Determination) and no identifiers_removed list; its own source_caveats concede the record 'does not state whether identifiable elements remain present in the released dataset'. data_protection_impacts is likewise absent.
recommendation: State the HIPAA compliance basis, name the de-identification determination applied (Safe Harbor or Expert Determination), and list the identifier classes removed or transformed per modality.

description: No persistent identifier is present. id is 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset', a project-website URL with a fragment rather than a DOI, ARK or Handle; doi, citation and rrid are absent, as source_caveats itself records ('no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation').
recommendation: Mint a DOI for the controlled-access release (metadata-only DOIs are standard for restricted clinical data) and add a recommended citation.

description: Two contact strings are malformed as published and reproduced verbatim: the maintainer email 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' (domain misspelled, flagged in the record's own source_caveats) and the external resource 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' recorded without a URL scheme. The notes field also reproduces the site banner misspelling 'repoitory'.
recommendation: Retain the verbatim source string but add a corrected, resolvable contact and URL alongside it so the record remains actionable.

description: conforms_to_standard collapses three distinct standards (EDF+, Persyst, the OHNLP open source schema) into a single OTHER enum term, and the WFDB term stands for a schema the source describes as extended rather than plain WFDB. The record discloses this, but the structured field understates the standards landscape.
recommendation: Either extend the enum or repeat each unmapped standard as a separate OTHER entry with its name carried in an accompanying free-text slot.

description: Two sources disagree on scale and the disagreement is carried into the scored values: tier-2 documentation gives 50,000 admissions and 7,642 admissions with radiology data, while the tier-4 August 2025 webinar gives 'over 45K unique admissions' and 1000 images. The record discloses the conflict and unit mismatch rather than concealing it, which is good practice, but the headline counts remain contested.
recommendation: Date-stamp each count to a named release snapshot so the two figures can be read as successive states rather than as a contradiction.

description: Temporal coverage of the clinical data is unstated. collection_timeframes gives the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 and its own source_caveats notes these 'are the NIH project period for award OT2OD032701, not the clinical period the admissions are drawn from'. Temporal ordering of collection, processing and publication therefore cannot be checked.
recommendation: State the admission date range covered by the released extract per contributing site.

description: No variable-level metadata is present. variables is absent for a release of 1.6 billion OMOP rows across nine modalities; OMOP CDM conformance supplies column semantics for the structured tables only, and nothing describes the flowsheet extensions, the OHNLP token schema, or the waveform channel inventory.
recommendation: Publish a data dictionary keyed to OMOP tables plus the local extensions, and a channel/label inventory for telemetry and EEG.

description: No download_url or platform link is recorded, and no publisher, citation or DOI. Access is reachable only through two personal email addresses in data_governance.access_review_process; the enclave hosting OMOP and telemetry data is described but never named or linked.
recommendation: Name the hosting platform/enclave with a request URL, and record a publisher and citation so the dataset is cross-referenceable.

description: No related_datasets or parent_datasets with typed relationships are recorded, even though the dataset is one of four Bridge2AI data generation projects and provisions a sequestered holdout test set that is a sibling of the released cohort.
recommendation: Add typed relationships to the sequestered holdout set and to the sibling Bridge2AI datasets.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true for a cohort of 50,000 critically ill hospital admissions, but no IRB, ethics committee, reviewing body, or approval identifier is named anywhere. The two ethical_reviews entries give 'CHoRUS consortium' as reviewing_organization and describe community ethics focus groups and an 'Ethics (Ethical and Trustworthy AI)' pillar; both carry source_caveats stating that no body performed a formal ethical review of the dataset. The prescribed check (involves_human_subjects=True implies IRB approval documented) fails.
recommendation: Add the reviewing IRB(s) of record for the contributing hospitals with protocol numbers and determination type (approved, exempt, or not-human-subjects determination for the coordinating center), and record any data protection impact assessment.

description: involves_human_subjects is true but there is no informed_consent field at all, and no waiver of consent is documented. direct_collection.is_direct is false ('extracted from hospital clinical systems ... rather than gathered directly from patients for research purposes'), which typically implies a waiver of consent or an authorization exception, yet neither is stated. A reuser cannot determine the consent basis on which the data were assembled.
recommendation: Add informed_consent recording the consent basis for retrospective extraction (IRB waiver of consent under 45 CFR 46.116, HIPAA waiver of authorization, or broad consent), including any withdrawal mechanism.

description: No DOI is present and the only identifier, id: 'https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset', is a fragment anchor on the project homepage. It is syntactically a URI but carries no persistence guarantee, is not registered with any resolver, and will not survive a site reorganization. The record's own source_caveats confirm: 'The bundle gives no release date, DOI, version identifier, or recommended citation for the dataset'.
recommendation: Mint a DOI through DataCite or the hosting repository and record it in doi, together with a recommended citation string.

description: The dataset is shared to external users (third_party_sharing.is_shared true; access granted to up to 30 AIM-AHEAD trainees) and its status is 'partially released' with an acknowledged expansion trajectory, yet there is no version field and no version_access. Users given access in different months will hold materially different data (imaging de-identification and EEG extraction were in process as of August 2025) with no identifier distinguishing what they received, which defeats reproducible citation.
recommendation: Assign a version identifier to each enclave snapshot and document in version_access how a user pins or retrieves a specific prior version.

description: is_deidentified.method describes concrete, modality-appropriate procedures (OHNLP tokenization, local retention of notes, imaging de-identification, transformations limiting re-identification) but names no recognized de-identification standard, and its source_caveats state the bundle 'does not state whether identifiable elements remain present in the released dataset'. For US hospital EHR, imaging and waveform data, regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is unset and no Safe Harbor or Expert Determination basis is claimed, so the regulatory status of the released data is indeterminate.
recommendation: State the de-identification basis (HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination, with the 18 identifier categories addressed) and set hipaa_compliant explicitly; note separately that DICOM header scrubbing and waveform metadata handling were covered.

description: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk does not assess risk; it restates mitigation ('The project transforms data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused ethics and legal work determines the approaches used to manage privacy'). No risk level, no residual-risk statement, and no consideration of the specific re-identification vectors this dataset carries (high-frequency waveforms, geocoded distance-to-hospital, rare NICU/PICU case mix at named academic centers).
recommendation: Replace the circular statement with an assessment of residual risk naming the quasi-identifiers of concern, notably geocoded location derived via DeGauss and long-duration waveform signatures.

description: Vulnerable populations are clearly identified in human_subject_research.special_populations ('pediatric intensive care (PICU) and neonatal intensive care (NICU) patients', acutely and critically ill patients), but no at_risk_populations entry describes protections specific to those groups, and participant_compensation is absent with no statement that compensation is inapplicable to retrospective extraction. Identification without safeguards leaves the strongest protection claim in the record unsupported.
recommendation: Add at_risk_populations describing the additional safeguards applied to pediatric and neonatal records (parental permission basis, assent where applicable, any extra access conditions), and state explicitly that no participant compensation applies to retrospective extraction.

description: There is no variables field. For a dataset of 1.6 billion OMOP rows plus flowsheet extensions, note tokens, waveforms and EEG, no variable-level metadata, data dictionary, or column identifiers are provided. Reliance on the OMOP CDM covers the standard tables but not the documented schema extensions for high-frequency nursing flowsheets, which are by definition non-standard.
recommendation: Publish a data dictionary, at minimum for the OMOP extension tables and the OHNLP token schema, with variable identifiers, types and permissible values.

description: No anomalies and no missing_data_documentation, and sampling_strategies contains two statements of intent rather than a protocol: 'Sampling at scale across data contributing centers...' and the future-tense 'Federated access will enable sampling methods to ensure a balanced and diverse cohort'. For multi-site EHR data with acknowledged uneven modality coverage, missingness patterns are a first-order quality concern and are not characterized.
recommendation: Document per-modality and per-site missingness rates, known data quality anomalies surfaced by the CHoRUSReports characterization reports, and the actual inclusion criteria and selection protocol used to reach 50,000 admissions.

description: Two sources disagree on dataset scale and the record discloses the conflict rather than resolving it: 50,000 admissions (tier-2 website) versus 'over 45K unique admissions' as of August 2025 (tier-4 webinar), and 7,642 admissions with radiology data versus 1000 images available. The record correctly notes the imaging figures use different units. The disclosure is good practice; the residual effect is that the released scale remains ambiguous to a planner.
recommendation: Publish a dated release manifest giving per-modality counts as of a stated snapshot, so a single authoritative figure supersedes the two conflicting sources.

description: collection_timeframes reports the NIH award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30 as the collection timeframe. The record's own source_caveats correctly identify this as a temporal mismatch: 'the admissions almost certainly predate the award, and the bundle does not state the temporal coverage of the clinical data'. Temporal ordering is therefore unverifiable, and a user cannot tell which care era the admissions reflect.
recommendation: State the admission date range of the clinical data, separately from the award period.

description: conforms_to_standard collapses three distinct standards (EDF+, Persyst, OHNLP open source schema) into a single OTHER term, and the WFDB entry stands for what the source describes as an extended rather than plain WFDB schema. The prose conforms_to field carries the full detail, so the loss is confined to the machine-readable enum; the record discloses it.
recommendation: Request enum terms for EDF+, Persyst and the OHNLP schema, or carry them in a free-text companion slot alongside OTHER so machine consumers are not misled.

description: One external_resources entry, 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus', lacks a URI scheme and is therefore not a dereferenceable URL. Separately, the maintainer contact address is given as 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu', with a misspelled domain. Both are reproduced faithfully from the source and flagged as such by the record, which is the correct transcription choice, but both are unusable as written.
recommendation: Retain the verbatim source value but add a corrected, resolvable form (https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus and the intended mgh.harvard.edu domain) marked as an editorial correction.

description: No publisher field and no recognized repository. The data sit in an unnamed 'cloud enclave' and the 'Bridge2AI AI/ML for Clinical Care Collaborative Cloud' is mentioned only in intended_uses and existing_uses prose. Combined with the absent DOI and citation, the dataset has no persistent platform identity in the wider ecosystem.
recommendation: Record the hosting platform as publisher and register the dataset with a recognized repository or catalog entry that carries a DOI, even if the data themselves remain in the controlled enclave.

description: There are no prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses. For a controlled-access dataset of identifiable-origin clinical records, the absence of an explicit prohibition on re-identification attempts and on redistribution is a notable asymmetry against the strong access controls documented elsewhere; the licensing agreement presumably contains such terms but its contents are not summarized.
recommendation: Summarize the licensing agreement's key prohibitions (no re-identification, no redistribution, no attempted contact with subjects) in prohibited_uses.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the cohort includes PICU and NICU patients, but no IRB, ethics committee, approval identifier, or waiver determination is documented. ethical_reviews names only the consortium itself as 'reviewing_organization' and its own source_caveats state that 'the bundle names no IRB, ethics committee, or approval identifier, and does not state that any body performed a formal ethical review of the dataset.'
recommendation: Add the reviewing IRB(s) of record for the coordinating centre and contributing sites with protocol/approval identifiers, or state explicitly that the retrospective extraction proceeded under an IRB waiver of consent and name the body that granted it.

description: involves_human_subjects is true but informed_consent is entirely absent. For a retrospective EHR/PACS/telemetry extraction a consent waiver is the expected disposition, yet neither consent procedures nor a waiver is recorded, leaving the consent basis for 50,000 admissions undocumented.
recommendation: Add an informed_consent entry stating the consent basis (e.g. IRB-approved waiver of informed consent under 45 CFR 46.116(f) for retrospective record review), including whether any site obtained prospective consent.

description: status is 'partially released' and updates.update_details describes an actively growing dataset (50,000 admissions now, 100,000 anticipated; imaging de-identification and EEG extraction in process), yet no version, version_access, or errata are recorded. A growing controlled-access dataset with no version label cannot support reproducible analyses.
recommendation: Assign and record a release version (e.g. v1.0, dated), document how prior versions are obtained from the enclave, and open an errata/change log alongside the roadmap already stated in updates.

description: The dataset is shared with external users under a signed licensing agreement (third_party_sharing.is_shared true; AIM-AHEAD trainees) but no DOI and no recommended citation exist, so reuse cannot be cited or cross-referenced. The record's own source_caveats confirm the gap.
recommendation: Mint a DOI for the released snapshot through a registrar (DataCite via the hosting enclave or a Bridge2AI repository) and publish a recommended citation string alongside the access instructions.

description: The only identifier is id: https://chorus4ai.org/#dataset, a fragment anchor on the project homepage. It is a syntactically valid URI but carries no persistence guarantee, no resolver, and no registrar; doi and RRID are absent.
recommendation: Replace or supplement the homepage-fragment id with a registered persistent identifier (DOI, ARK, or Handle) and record an RRID if the resource is registered with SciCrunch.

description: Deidentification is described as activity (OHNLP tokenization, local note retention, image de-identification in process, 'approaches that limit re-identification') but no formal standard is named. For US hospital PHI the expected dispositions are HIPAA Safe Harbor or Expert Determination; neither is stated, and is_deidentified.source_caveats concede that whether identifiable elements remain is unrecorded.
recommendation: State the de-identification standard applied per modality (Safe Harbor vs Expert Determination), list the identifier classes removed or transformed, and record HIPAA compliance status in regulatory_restrictions.

description: participant_privacy.reidentification_risk restates mitigation rather than assessing risk: 'The project transforms data using approaches that limit re-identification, and patient-focused ethics and legal work determines the approaches used to manage privacy.' No residual risk level, no quantification, no adversary model. data_protection_impacts is absent although confidentiality_level is 'restricted'.
recommendation: Record an explicit residual re-identification risk assessment (method, assumptions, residual risk level) and attach a data protection impact assessment for the waveform, imaging, and geospatial SDOH elements, which are the highest-risk modalities here.

description: No variable-level metadata exists anywhere in the record (variables absent), despite 1.6 billion rows of OMOP data with documented schema extensions for nursing flowsheets. OMOP conformance defines the base tables, but the extensions and the waveform/EEG channel semantics are undocumented.
recommendation: Publish a data dictionary covering the OMOP extension tables for nursing flowsheets, the OHNLP token schema fields, and waveform/EEG channel labels and units.

description: Missing-data and anomaly documentation is absent (anomalies, missing_data_documentation, imputation_protocols all unpopulated) even though the record itself establishes severe modality sparsity: 7,642 of 50,000 admissions have radiology, EEG extraction is in process, and only note tokens are centralised.
recommendation: Document per-modality coverage rates and missingness patterns, known anomalies in waveform capture and OMOP mapping, and state explicitly that no imputation is performed if that is the case.

description: The two source tiers disagree on scale (50,000 vs 'over 45K' admissions; 7,642 admissions-with-radiology vs 1000 images). The record adjudicates the conflict transparently at source_caveats and on each affected instance, so the disagreement is disclosed rather than concealed; the imaging figures remain in incommensurable units.
recommendation: Report imaging availability in one consistent unit (studies and admissions with imaging) with an as-of date, and timestamp the admission count.

description: is_tabular is false for a dataset whose largest component is 1.6 billion rows of OMOP tabular data. The flag is defensible at the multimodal dataset level but is semantically ambiguous where tabular and non-tabular modalities coexist.

description: Two URI/address defects are carried through from the sources and flagged as such by the record: the external resource 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' lacks a URL scheme, and the maintainer contact domain reads 'mgh.havard.edu' (Harvard misspelt, and MGH's domain is mgh.harvard.edu). description: collection_timeframes gives the NIH award period (2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30) rather than the clinical period the admissions are drawn from, and the record states so. Temporal coverage of the EHR data is therefore unknown, which affects drift and secular-trend analyses.

description: No related_datasets or parent_datasets with typed relationships are recorded, although the record describes a sequestered holdout set derived from the same cohort and situates CHoRUS among four Bridge2AI data generation projects.
recommendation: Express the holdout set and sibling Bridge2AI datasets as typed relationships (isPartOf, hasPart, isSiblingOf) rather than prose.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true for a multicenter dataset of 50,000 ICU/PICU/NICU admissions, but no IRB approval, ethics board of record, or data protection impact assessment is documented. recommendation: Add the IRB or reliance-agreement of record (institution, protocol number, approval or waiver status) for the retrospective multi-site extraction, and record any DPIA performed for the cloud enclave.

description: involves_human_subjects=true but informed_consent is entirely absent. For retrospective EHR/waveform/imaging extraction a consent waiver is the expected documentation, and neither consent nor waiver is recorded.
recommendation: State whether consent was obtained, waived under 45 CFR 46.116(f), or handled by site-specific arrangement, and describe any withdrawal mechanism.

description: is_deidentified.method claims tokenization and 'transformation of data using approaches that limit re-identification', and sensitive_elements flags patient-level clinical data including waveforms, imaging, notes and social determinants of health, yet participant_privacy and an explicit re-identification risk assessment are absent. description: The deidentification method is described procedurally (tokenization, CTP-deid, privacy_scan_tool, imaging de-id in process) but no recognized standard is named (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity), and no HIPAA compliance status is recorded anywhere despite US hospital PHI being the source.

description: No persistent identifier: doi is absent and id is the project homepage https://chorus4ai.org/, which is a web address rather than a DOI, RRID, ARK or Handle. Correspondingly no citation and no publisher are recorded, so the dataset cannot be cited or cross-referenced.
recommendation: Mint a DOI for the released snapshot, name the hosting platform in publisher, and supply a recommended citation string.

description: No variable-level metadata at all: variables is absent, is_tabular is unset, and no data dictionary is referenced, despite 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular data. description: license_and_use_terms documents only the AIM-AHEAD training-programme licensing agreement and explicitly notes that no general license for the data is stated; there are also no prohibited_uses or discouraged_uses for a sensitive clinical corpus.
recommendation: State the data use agreement that governs general controlled access and enumerate prohibited uses (re-identification attempts, redistribution, clinical deployment without validation).

description: No version, version_access or errata, and no download_url. A dataset described as partially released and growing from 50,000 toward 100,000 admissions has no way for a user to name or retrieve the snapshot they used.

description: known_biases and future_use_impacts are absent, and anomalies and missing_data_documentation are absent, for a multi-site retrospective EHR corpus where site-mix bias and structured missingness are near-certain. Bias is mentioned only obliquely inside ethical_reviews and intended_uses.

description: The maintainer contact is 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu', whose domain is misspelled ('havard' for 'harvard', and MGH's domain is mgh.harvard.edu). description: Two internally inconsistent counts are reported for the cohort (50,000 admissions on chorus4ai.org versus over 45K as of August 2025 in the webinar) and for imaging (7,642 admissions versus roughly 1,000 images). description: The record describes patient-level hospital data from 14 contributing hospitals (description: 'retrospective, controlled-access clinical data on critically ill patients'), yet human_subject_research is unpopulated and ethical_reviews names no IRB, ethics committee approval or protocol number. description: subpopulations and description both state that pediatric ICU and neonatal ICU admissions are included, which are minors and a canonical at-risk population, but at_risk_populations is unpopulated and no assent or guardian-permission arrangements are described. description: is_deidentified.method names techniques (OHNLP tokenization, imaging de-identification, transformations that limit re-identification) but no recognized standard (HIPAA Safe Harbor, Expert Determination, k-anonymity) and no list of identifier categories removed. description: No re-identification risk assessment and no data_protection_impacts, despite three risk-amplifying design choices documented elsewhere in the record: geocoding of OMOP Location entities via DeGauss, retention of high-resolution physiologic waveforms and EEG, and linkage of nine modalities at the admission level.

description: The dataset is asserted to be shared and reusable (third_party_sharing.is_shared=true, five populated distribution_formats, a provisioned holdout test set), yet there is no download_url, no publisher, no doi, no citation and no version. description: The title frames the resource as being 'for Equitable AI' and keywords include 'social determinants of health', but known_biases is entirely absent. description: The only identifier is id='https://chorus4ai.org/#chorus-dataset', a fragment on the project homepage.
