recommendation: Record the HIPAA compliance status and pathway explicitly, plus any state-level or institutional frameworks governing the enclave.

description: license_and_use_terms describes an access gate (controlled access, a licensing agreement inside a training-program registration form, a '.edu' email requirement) but never states reuse rights: no license identifier, no redistribution, attribution, derivative-work or publication terms for the data. description: The published program-manager contact 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains an apparent domain typo ('havard'). The record transparently marks it 'as published', but as recorded the primary project contact address is likely undeliverable.

recommendation: Mint a DOI (or ARK/Handle) for the released dataset version and use a dataset-scoped URI for id, distinct from the project landing page.

description: license_and_use_terms conflates two distinct objects: the MIT License applies to the chorus-ai code, while no license is named for the data. description: No regulatory determination is recorded for a US multicenter clinical dataset: regulatory_restrictions carries confidentiality_level 'restricted' and access-control statements but no HIPAA status, no other_compliance entries, and no governance committee contact of record (contacts appear only as individual emails under maintainers and data_governance.access_review_process).

description: No variable-level metadata anywhere: variables and is_tabular are absent, despite 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular EHR data being the largest component of the release. description: Several capabilities are documented in fields that ordinarily describe realized dataset properties but are stated in the future tense: splits (a holdout test set the award abstract says will be provisioned) and labeling_strategies (an annotation environment that 'will label data'). description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the cohort includes pediatric and neonatal ICU admissions, but there is no informed_consent block at all: no consent procedure, no waiver of consent, no HIPAA authorization statement, and no parental permission/assent discussion. direct_collection.is_direct=false explains that data were not collected from individuals for this purpose, which is relevant context but is not consent documentation.

description: The dataset is PHI-derived clinical data from 14 US hospitals, yet no regulatory framework is asserted: regulatory_restrictions, confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are all absent. description: No persistent identifier exists. doi is absent, no RRID is present, and id is https://chorus4ai.org/ — byte-identical to the page value and resolving to the project homepage rather than to this dataset. description: status is 'released' and distribution_dates reports a dataset available to approved users as of August 2025, but version, version_access, errata, citation, doi and publisher are all absent. description: The dataset's dominant component is 1.6 billion rows of OMOP-standardized tabular EHR data, yet variables is absent, is_tabular is absent, and no data dictionary is provided. subsets name content categories (demographics, medications, procedures, flowsheets, diagnoses) but carry no variable-level metadata or identifiers.

The download_url slot is empty; access is conveyed through distribution_formats.access_urls, one of which is the landing page and the other the Dataverse data-access API base https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, which is a truncated endpoint requiring a file identifier that the record does not supply for any of the ten archives. The errata slot is likewise empty, and there is no consolidated release-level changelog; what changed since the October 2025 release has to be reconstructed from source_caveats.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the resolvable landing or access URL, list the Dataverse file identifiers so the API pattern is usable, and add an errata or release-notes entry summarising what changed in the June 2026 release.

description: Two disclosed but unresolved source conditions sit in tension with other assertions. First, the CM4AI portal's 'Released on: June 17, 2025' against the Dataverse publication date of 2026-06-17 is a one-year discrepancy that the record resolves by source ranking without reconciling; the internal dates it does assert (created_on 2025-02-27, issued 2026-06-17, distribution_dates 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-15) are mutually ordered and consistent. Second, notes records that the hosting Dataverse collection 'is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives', which is an availability risk that retention_limit's commitment to 'long term preservation ... supported by committed institutional funds' does not acknowledge.
recommendation: Note in retention_limit that the hosting collection is under review, so that the preservation commitment is read alongside the disclosed risk to it.

description: imputation_protocols is absent and is not documented as unused. missing_data_documentation describes what is missing from the release and why, but does not state whether any imputation was performed on the released mass-spectrometry or single-cell data, where missing values are routine.
recommendation: Add an imputation_protocols entry stating either the imputation method applied to missing quantitative values or that no imputation was performed.

description: Temporal ordering is internally contradictory: the dataset is issued 2026-06-17, yet three immunofluorescence archives carry issued: 2026-07-15, a month after the version publication date, and created_on is 2025-02-27, sixteen months before issuance. The record flags the file-date anomaly in source_caveats but supplies no resolution.
recommendation: State explicitly whether the July 2026 immunofluorescence archives were added in a post-publication Dataverse revision, and record that revision in an errata or update entry.

description: Two upstream sources disagree on the release date (CM4AI portal: 'Released on: June 17, 2025'; UVA Dataverse: Publication Date 2026-06-17). The record adopts the Dataverse date and documents the conflict, which is good practice, but the dataset title ('June 2026') and the portal listing remain mutually inconsistent for any user arriving from the portal.
recommendation: Retain the conflict note and additionally record which source was consulted on what date, so downstream users can re-verify.

description: No variable-level metadata at all: variables, is_tabular, is_data_split and is_subpopulation are entirely absent, and the ten ZIP archives carry no per-file content description. A reuser cannot determine what columns, channels or matrices the archives contain without downloading them.
recommendation: Add variables entries (or a data dictionary reference) for the perturb-seq cell atlas matrix and the SEC-MS/AP-MS elution and interaction tables, and set is_tabular where applicable.

description: Distribution format is declared only as the ZIP container (format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip) for all ten archives. ZIP is packaging, not a data format: the record never states whether the contents are mzML, TIFF/OME-TIFF, h5ad, MTX, FASTQ or CSV. This satisfies the distribution question but not the interoperability question.
recommendation: Describe the internal file formats and character encoding of each archive alongside the ZIP container declaration.

description: Reported sample magnitudes cannot be attributed to this release. The portal 'Data Insights' figures (53,788 images, 11,739 genes, 21.4 TB) are read by the record as cumulative project-wide holdings by inference, and the 523-protein figure conflicts with the 464-protein figure on the October 2025 release page. The record correctly declines to assert either for the June 2026 archives, leaving instance counts for this release unstated.
recommendation: Report per-release counts (images, targeted genes, proteins, cells) for the ten archives actually distributed here, or state that they are not published.

description: No software that produced or transformed the distributed archives is named. The Cell Mapping Toolkit / CM4AI integration pipeline is named, but the record states the computed cell maps it produces are explicitly not included in this release; FAIRSCAPE is named for packaging, metadata and provenance-graph production. Neither answers what generated the SEC-MS, AP-MS, immunofluorescence or perturb-seq atlas products that are distributed.
recommendation: Name and version the acquisition and processing software for each modality (e.g. mass-spectrometry search engine, image acquisition/segmentation pipeline, CellRanger or equivalent for the CRISPRi atlas).

description: Preprocessing is documented only as an inference from archive names ('Inferred from the paired archive names ... the June 2026 release listing carries no per-file processing description'), and no cleaning, labeling, annotation-quality or imputation documentation exists. The atlas is known to be a processed product but not how it was processed.
recommendation: Document the CRISPRi atlas processing pipeline (alignment, guide assignment, QC filtering, normalization) and state explicitly whether imputation was used.

description: Governance is partly aspirational relative to the release as distributed: data_governance.notes reports a Data Access Committee as a planned arrangement in the preprint, while all ten archives are listed with public file access; and the commercial-licensing and copyright statements in ip_restrictions are drawn from the preprint and earlier release pages rather than from the June 2026 page, which states only CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
recommendation: Confirm on the current release page whether the dual-licensing and Stanford/UCSF copyright carve-outs still apply to the June 2026 archives.

description: Ethical review contact identity is reconciled across sources with a residual mismatch: Vardit Ravitsky is given affiliation University of Montreal while the contact email domain is thehastingscenter.org. The record discloses the mismatch rather than silently resolving it.
recommendation: Record the affiliation associated with the governance role rather than the authorship affiliation, or note that both are current.

description: No errata and no version-level change log. updates describes only a forward-looking quarterly cadence; the one comparative statement ('adds AP-MS data for treated MDA-MB-468 ... which the October 2025 release did not include') sits in related_datasets.notes and describes a cross-DOI delta, not what changed between Dataverse versions of this DOI. The carried-forward '(2025-06-30)' description stamp and the differing MD5s for same-named October 2025 archives are exactly the kind of item an errata entry should carry.
recommendation: Add an errata list and a per-version change description covering the AP-MS addition, the July 2026 file additions, the checksum changes and the stale description stamp.

description: No downstream social impact analysis (future_use_impacts) and no conflict-of-interest statement, despite a named ethics team and an explicit ethics workstream in the project's stated purposes ('ethical, AI-ready datasets').
recommendation: Record the substance of the ethics workstream's review — anticipated downstream impacts of cell-architecture models and mitigations — not only the contacts responsible for it.

description: sampling_strategies[1].is_sample: false is the record's own reading of 'expressed genome-scale' and 'whole-genome', which the record admits no source states in terms. A false flag asserted on inference is weaker evidence than the surrounding prose it rests on.
recommendation: Prefer leaving the boolean unset where the source does not support it, and retain the prose description.

description: The single erratum is self-referential: 'The June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release'. The related_datasets chain indicates the June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, published 2025-07-01) revised the March 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, published 2025-03-03), so the antecedent release name appears to be wrong.
recommendation: Correct the erratum text to name the March 2025 release as the revised predecessor, or state explicitly which pair of releases the erratum describes.

description: Version numbering is non-monotonic across the release chain: the top-level version for this June 2026 release is '2.0', while version_access records the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases as version 2.1. A successor release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors is implausible and will confuse automated version ordering.
recommendation: Reconcile the version string with the Dataverse version history, or add a note distinguishing the Dataverse draft/major version label ('V2') from the semantic release version.

description: No software is named that produced or transformed the data actually distributed in this release. The named tooling is either capture instrumentation (10x Genomics 3'HT kit, pipetting robot, confocal microscopy), metadata/packaging production (FAIRSCAPE), hosting and sharing (NDEx, MassIVE, Figshare), or a pipeline the record itself states produced outputs not present here (MuSIC / Cell Mapping Toolkit, IMP, node2vec, the HPA deep-learning image model). A reuser cannot determine what software generated the ten archives.
recommendation: Name, with versions, the acquisition-to-archive software that produced the released files (e.g. mass-spectrometry search/quantification software for the AP-MS and SEC-MS packages, the CellRanger or equivalent pipeline for perturb-seq, and the imaging export/conversion software), using used_software on the relevant processing strategies.

description: Every distributed file is described only as a ZIP container (format: ZIP, media_type: application/zip); no internal data format (e.g. mzML, mzTab, TIFF/OME-TIFF, h5ad, MTX, FASTQ/SRA) and no character encoding is documented for any archive.
recommendation: Document the internal file formats and encodings of each archive, so a reuser can tell what to parse before a multi-gigabyte download.

description: No variable-level metadata is provided anywhere in the record: the variables slot is absent entirely, so the columns, channels and measured fields inside the mass-spectrometry, perturb-seq and image archives are undocumented.
recommendation: Add variable metadata (or a pointer to a per-modality data dictionary inside the RO-Crate) with identifiers and descriptions for the tabular outputs in each archive.

description: No data anomalies, sampling strategies, or missing-data documentation are recorded. The anomalies, sampling_strategies and missing_data_documentation slots are all absent; the extensive source_caveats concern disagreements between metadata sources, not quality issues in the data themselves.
recommendation: Document known data-level quality issues (failed replicates, low-confidence identifications, out-of-focus fields, dropout in single-cell libraries) and how missing values are represented.

description: No processing of the released data is documented: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools and imputation_protocols are all absent, and notes explicitly scope the MuSIC pipeline description to tooling and future releases rather than to these files.
recommendation: Describe the processing each modality's released archive underwent between instrument output and deposit, even where that processing is minimal, and state explicitly where no processing was applied.

description: Instance-level counts are not reported for this release: the instances entries carry no counts of images, cells, proteins or interactions, and the record's own source_caveats note that the June 2026 listing states no protein count. Quantification is available only at file level (10 files, 12,601,718,300 bytes).
recommendation: Report per-modality instance counts (images per condition, cells per perturb-seq library, proteins assayed) for this release once the source listing supports them.

description: The stated maintenance horizon and the recorded funding period do not align: updates.update_details promises quarterly updates 'through the end of the project in November 2026', while the funders notes give the NIH project period as 2022-09-01 to 2026-08-31.
recommendation: State whether the project end date reflects a no-cost extension or a separate supplement period, or align the two dates.

description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is recoverable only from distribution_formats.access_urls, page and publisher, all of which carry the same Dataverse landing-page URL; no per-file retrieval endpoint or Data Access API base URL is given despite the API being mentioned in prose.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the Dataverse Data Access API endpoint and, where possible, per-file access URLs keyed to the recorded file identifiers.

description: No future_use_impacts (rai:dataSocialImpact) analysis and no conflict-of-interest statement accompany the ethical review, so anticipated downstream social impacts of the released maps and their mitigations are undocumented.
recommendation: Add a future_use_impacts entry covering anticipated downstream social impacts of AI models trained on these data and the mitigations the Ethics module envisages.

description: Only one bias is categorized (representation_bias, cell lines not representing population variation). Plausible biases specific to the modalities — antibody-availability bias in the immunofluorescence protein panel, detectability bias in SEC-MS/AP-MS toward abundant and soluble complexes, guide-library coverage bias in the CRISPRi screen — are not categorized.
recommendation: Add typed bias entries for antibody/panel selection, mass-spectrometry detectability, and CRISPR library coverage.

description: The two ethical_reviews entries carry byte-identical review_details prose, differing only in contact_person, and describe an oversight role rather than a completed review with a date, determination or reference. data_protection_impacts is absent.
recommendation: Record the determination itself (who reviewed what, when, and with what outcome) rather than restating the oversight remit once per contact.

description: Seven of the ten file collections are typed collection_type: processed_data, but no preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, annotation_analyses, machine_annotation_tools or imputation_protocols are present. A reader cannot tell how raw AP-MS, SEC-MS or perturb-seq output became the distributed processed archives.
recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies and cleaning_strategies entries describing the per-modality pipelines (spectral search and quantification for MS, alignment and guide assignment for perturb-seq, image QC for IF) that produced the archives marked processed_data.

description: No software is named as having produced or transformed the data actually distributed. The tools the record does name fall outside that role: the Cell Mapping Toolkit / MuSIC pipeline is stated by the record itself to produce computed cell maps that 'are not included in this release'; FAIRSCAPE is packaging and provenance-metadata software; NDEx and the UVA Dataverse are sharing and hosting platforms; the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit is acquisition instrumentation.
recommendation: Name the processing software and versions that produced each released archive (for example the MS search/quantification engine, CellRanger or equivalent for the perturb-seq reads, and the image processing toolchain), with repository or DOI links.

description: No variable-level metadata is provided for any subset; the variables slot is entirely absent, so column, channel and measurement semantics inside the ZIP archives are undocumented.
recommendation: Add variables entries (or per-collection data dictionaries) describing at minimum the MS elution-profile table columns, the perturb-seq atlas matrix fields, and the IF image channel-to-target mapping.

description: distribution_formats declares only the container: format ZIP with media_type application/zip. The scientific payload formats inside the archives (image format for the 12.6 GB of IF data, mass-spectrometry table or mzML-family format, perturb-seq matrix format) and character encoding are never stated, which limits interoperability and harmonization.
recommendation: Record the internal file formats and encodings per file collection in addition to the ZIP container, for example OME-TIFF for imaging and TSV/UTF-8 for the elution profile tables.

description: No instance or sample counts are reported at release level: instances lists four instance types with no counts, and source_caveats explicitly declines to assert the project-level totals (1,374 interactions, 53,788 images, 11,739 genes) as release totals. total_file_count: 10 counts archives, not samples.
recommendation: State per-modality counts for this release (images, proteins/baits, guides and cells, elution fractions), even as approximate figures derived from the deposited archives.

description: No change log or errata for this release: errata is absent and updates carries only a forward-looking cadence ('quarterly ... through the end of the project in November 2026'). What changed relative to the October 2025 release can only be inferred from related_datasets notes.
recommendation: Add an errata or release-notes entry stating the delta for V2.0 (notably the addition of AP-MS data for paclitaxel- and vorinostat-treated MDA-MB-468 and the July 15 2026 addition of the three IF image archives).

description: No data anomalies, outliers, batch effects or missing-data documentation are recorded: anomalies and missing_data_documentation are both absent, even though the release spans four assay modalities with partially overlapping protein coverage.
recommendation: Document known quality issues per modality (failed baits, low-confidence guides, out-of-focus or discarded images) and how missingness across the incompletely overlapping protein sets should be handled.

description: The only access URL given is a truncated Dataverse API root, https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/, with no datafile identifier appended, so it does not resolve to any downloadable object; the dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the DOI-resolved dataset landing page and give per-collection access URLs including the datafile identifiers.

description: The conforms_to RO-Crate claim is, by the record's own admission, carried from the tier-3 preprint and the March/June 2025 releases: 'the June 2026 release page does not itself restate the packaging format, and its file listing names only cm4ai_release_metadata.zip without stating its internal format.' The conformance assertion is therefore unverified for the version being described.
recommendation: Confirm and state the packaging format of cm4ai_release_metadata.zip for V2.0, or scope the RO-Crate claim to the releases in which it was asserted.

description: Inherited date anomalies are disclosed but unresolved: the release page's Dataset Description block is dated 2025-06-30 on a release published 2026-06-17, and created_on 2025-02-27 is 'reused verbatim from earlier releases'. Top-level ordering (created_on 2025-02-27 < issued 2026-06-17 < last_updated_on 2026-07-15) is itself consistent.
recommendation: Correct or annotate the creation date so it reflects this release's data generation window rather than the collection's first deposit.

description: The KOLF2.1J line is described as 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' available via HipSci, i.e. donor-derived human material, while human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false. The determination is defensible for an established, distributed line, but the consent and ethical provenance of the originating donation are not referenced.
recommendation: Cite the HipSci/ATCC consent and ethical-sourcing provenance for the originating cell lines to close the chain of custody, without changing the human-subjects determination.

description: Regulatory metadata is thin on the classification axis: confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated; regulatory_restrictions records only 'FDA Regulated: No; no export control or regulatory restriction is stated'. Anticipated downstream social impacts (future_use_impacts) are likewise absent despite a substantial ethics programme.
recommendation: Add an explicit confidentiality classification (public/open for this CC BY-NC-SA release) and a future_use_impacts entry capturing the Ethics Module's anticipated social impacts of AI-ready cell maps.

description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period, which does not reconcile with the four-year phased IRB protocol also summarized in the same block (pilot collection begun November 2023, still ongoing November 2024) or with the six documented releases spanning November 2024 to May 2026. The record surfaces the conflict in its own source_caveats rather than concealing it, which is good documentation practice, but the collection window of the released data remains undetermined.
recommendation: State the collection window for the v3.1.0 cohort explicitly (first and last session dates), and record the wider study period separately, so the 12-month figure is scoped rather than in tension.

description: confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, asserting no legally privileged data, while the same block's source_caveats and regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance both record that the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas. A CoC is a legal protection over the data, so the false flag reads more absolutely than the surrounding prose supports.
recommendation: Scope the false flag to the released feature set, or set the flag true and use confidentiality_details to distinguish the public features from the CoC-covered identifiable data held at sites.

description: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions states 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset', yet HIPAA de-identification rules, a Certificate of Confidentiality, PhysioNet credentialing requirements and a signed DUA all constrain the data and are documented in adjacent fields. The sweeping 'or other regulatory restrictions' clause contradicts the record's own compliance inventory.
recommendation: Narrow the statement to export controls specifically, since the other regulatory frameworks are already itemized in other_compliance and hipaa_compliant.

description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). It omits the disease cohorts the dataset is organized around (voice disorders, Parkinson's/neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory), the modalities (speech, cough, breathing), the methods (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic biomarker, machine learning) and the standards (BIDS) that a searcher would plausibly use.
recommendation: Expand to at least 8-12 keywords spanning modality, disease cohorts, feature families and standards; the description already contains the vocabulary to draw on.

description: variables declares only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames). These correctly document the join keys of the Parquet feature files, but the phenotype tables the record itself enumerates (confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires, task metadata) have no variable-level entries here, and are covered only by the statement that JSON data dictionaries ship alongside the TSVs.
recommendation: Either enumerate the principal phenotype variables or cite the specific data dictionary files by path so the external dictionaries are dereferenceable from the datasheet.

description: Several dedicated schema slots are unpopulated even though their substance is documented in prose elsewhere: publisher (PhysioNet is identified in citation, page, maintainers and third_party_sharing), download_url (access_urls and the DACO/credentialing process are given, and the absence of a file endpoint is explicitly and correctly explained by the access gating), is_tabular, imputation_protocols (no-imputation is stated in missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy), was_derived_from (derivation is carried by raw_data_sources and preprocessing_strategies), and media_type/encoding on the distribution formats. This costs machine-readability rather than human comprehension.
recommendation: Populate the dedicated slots with the values already present in prose; retain the prose explanations, which are the more informative part.

description: The RRID carried in the citation, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed and resolves to PhysioNet, the hosting repository, rather than to the dataset itself. Using a repository RRID inside a dataset citation is a category slip: it identifies where the data sit, not the resource being cited.
recommendation: Keep the DOI as the dataset identifier and either drop the repository RRID from the citation string or label it explicitly as the hosting platform's RRID.

description: The record documents five divergent renderings of the same NIH award across upstream sources (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3, 1OT2OD032720-01 and the malformed '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2'). The two renderings actually adopted into funders.grants are both well-formed NIH strings, and the malformed variant is quarantined in source_caveats rather than propagated, which is the correct handling; the underlying upstream inconsistency nonetheless remains unresolved.
recommendation: Cite the NIH RePORTER core project number as canonical and list the supplement application numbers beneath it, noting the documentation footer string as a typographical error in the source.

description: The description lists pediatric voice and speech disorders among the five cohort categories recruited, while human_subject_research.special_populations and subpopulations state that pediatric participants are released as a separate dataset and that this release contains adults only. The two statements are reconcilable (five consortium cohorts versus one adult release) but the description does not make the scoping explicit at the point where it lists the cohorts.
recommendation: Add a clause to the description noting that the pediatric cohort is recruited under the same consortium protocol but published as the companion pediatric dataset.

description: The recording-count evidence is inconsistent across upstream sources: approximately 61,937 voice-derived recordings from 833 participants in the project documentation against per-feature counts on PhysioNet (32,522 pitch series, 29,278 spectrograms, 29,289 posteriorgram files). The record resolves this by preferring the higher-ranked source and declining to state a single recording total, which is defensible, but the audio-recording instance entry consequently carries no count.
recommendation: Record the per-feature counts as structured values on the audio recording instance so the absence of a single total is visibly a deliberate choice rather than a gap.

description: keywords contains only four terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice), all of them generic programme- or domain-level labels. None of the five disease cohort categories, none of the acoustic-feature or processing methods (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram, BIDS), and none of the modality terms (speech, cough, breathing) that the description itself uses are exposed as search terms.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering the disease cohorts (voice disorders, Parkinson disease, mood disorders, respiratory disorders), the modalities (speech, cough, breathing), the derived feature families (spectrogram, MFCC, phonetic posteriorgram) and the standards (BIDS, FHIR).

description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated while the dataset is demonstrably distributed: distribution_formats.access_urls carry the PhysioNet landing page and the Synapse controlled-access page, and the notes explain that no file endpoint is published because the files are gated. The access route is therefore documented, but a consumer reading the download_url field alone would find nothing.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the gated PhysioNet files endpoint (or repeat the landing page there) and keep the existing note explaining that credentialing precedes retrieval.

description: The publisher slot is not populated. PhysioNet is identified unambiguously in the citation string, in page, in third_party_sharing and in maintainers, so the hosting platform is recoverable, but no single field states it.
recommendation: Add publisher: PhysioNet (MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology), retaining Health Data Nexus as the publisher of the superseded version 1.0.

description: variables enumerates only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), all of them from the Parquet feature files. The release also ships phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata, whose variables are not enumerated; the record points to accompanying JSON data dictionaries instead.
recommendation: Either enumerate representative phenotype-table variables (at minimum the gold-standard diagnosis variables renamed in version 3.1.0) or cite the JSON data dictionaries explicitly from variables so the pointer is machine-followable.

description: is_tabular is not set although the release consists of Apache Parquet feature tables and tab-separated phenotype tables, and variables are declared with data types.
recommendation: Set is_tabular: true for the feature and phenotype distributions.

description: data_protection_impacts is not populated even though the record classifies the data as restricted, asserts HIPAA compliance, and carries a Certificate of Confidentiality. The substance of an impact assessment is present in participant_privacy.reidentification_risk and in the ethics working group's memorandum on controlled access to raw voice, so the gap is a missing dedicated slot rather than missing analysis.
recommendation: Record the ethics working group memorandum as a data_protection_impacts entry so the impact assessment is discoverable under its own field.

description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period, which does not reconcile with an IRB protocol describing a four-year phased study with pilot collection from November 2023 and with releases running from November 2024 to May 2026. The record discloses this conflict itself in collection_timeframes.source_caveats and states which source it preferred and why, so the disagreement is transparent rather than concealed.
recommendation: Where the sources do not settle the window, state a bounded range (e.g. 2023-11 to 2025) alongside the documentation figure rather than a bare duration.

description: The grant renderings are internally inconsistent across the underlying sources: OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3, 1OT2OD032720-01 and '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2'. The last is malformed for an NIH award. The two renderings actually asserted in funders.grants (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1) both parse correctly as NIH activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720, so the award identification itself validates; the variants are recorded only in source_caveats as a disclosed source discrepancy.
recommendation: Keep the two validating renderings in funders.grants and explicitly mark '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' in source_caveats as an apparent typographic corruption in the documentation footer.

description: confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, asserting that no data are covered by legal privilege, while regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance records a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas. These are reconcilable (the CoC protects against compelled disclosure rather than making the released features privileged) and the record flags the tension in its own source_caveats, but the boolean read alone understates the legal posture.
recommendation: Qualify confidential_elements_present with the CoC scope in confidentiality_details so the boolean is not read in isolation.

description: The description reproduces the consortium's own AI-readiness self-assessment percentages (100 percent FAIRness, 100 percent ethics, 50 percent sustainability, and so on). These are self-reported scores, attributed as such in the text, and the corresponding shortfalls are restated as limitations; they are nonetheless promotional in register for a description field.
recommendation: Move the self-assessment scorecard into an external_resources or notes entry and keep description focused on dataset content.

description: Internal tension inside the regulatory_restrictions block: the nested regulatory_restrictions list asserts 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual instances', while the sibling other_compliance field in the same block records a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against court orders and subpoenas, mandatory administrative/physical/technical safeguards, a five-business-day breach-reporting duty and PhysioNet-specific requirements, and confidentiality_level is 'restricted' with hipaa_compliant 'compliant'. A reader cannot tell from the block alone whether regulatory constraints apply.
recommendation: Narrow the negative statement to its intended scope (e.g. 'No export-control restrictions apply') so it does not contradict the Certificate of Confidentiality, HIPAA and PhysioNet obligations recorded in other_compliance.

description: confidential_elements_present is set to false on the grounds that the dataset contains no data protected by legal privilege or doctor-patient confidentiality, yet the same entry's source_caveats records that 'the underlying data are covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality', and the release carries clinician-assigned diagnostic labels derived from clinical interviews and electronic health records. The boolean and the caveat point in opposite directions.
recommendation: Either set confidential_elements_present to true and scope the detail to the de-identified release, or state explicitly that the flag refers only to the released feature tables and not to the underlying clinical source data.

description: keywords contains only four terms ('health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice'). The description covers speech, breathing and cough modalities, five named disease cohorts, BIDS, Parquet, acoustic feature families and machine-learning use, none of which are discoverable as keywords. Searchability is materially weaker than the record's own content warrants.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least eight to twelve terms covering modality (speech, cough, respiratory sounds), conditions (voice disorders, neurodegenerative, psychiatric, respiratory, pediatric), methods (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic biomarkers, machine learning) and standards (BIDS).

description: variables lists only four entries (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), all of them generic columns of the feature Parquet files. The phenotype tables the record itself enumerates - confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires, task metadata - are not described at variable level, so the analytically substantive columns have no variable metadata in the datasheet. is_tabular is also unset despite a release consisting of Parquet and TSV tables.
recommendation: Set is_tabular and extend variables to cover the phenotype table columns, or reference the shipped JSON data dictionaries as the authoritative variable list with a per-table summary in the datasheet.

description: The dedicated publisher slot is absent. The publishing platform is nevertheless identified unambiguously in citation ('PhysioNet'), maintainers ('PhysioNet, maintained by the MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, hosts the current dataset versions'), third_party_sharing and the page URL, so the sub-element's question is answered, but not from the field the rubric names.
recommendation: Populate publisher with 'PhysioNet (MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology)' so platform identification is machine-readable rather than only recoverable from prose.

description: download_url is unpopulated. The record explains why - 'No direct download URL is published: the PhysioNet files are gated behind credentialing and a signed data use agreement' - and supplies access_urls plus a full access_review_process, so the access route is documented even though the slot is empty.
recommendation: Record the credentialed-access endpoint or the request-form URL in download_url so automated harvesters can resolve an access route without parsing notes.

description: data_governance.committee_contact is not used; the governance contact address DACO@b2ai-voice.org appears instead in data_governance.stewardship_roles, raw_data_sources.access_details and maintainers. The contact is discoverable but not in the dedicated slot the rubric names for governance contacts.
recommendation: Set data_governance.committee_contact to DACO@b2ai-voice.org alongside the existing committee_name.

description: imputation_protocols and data_protection_impacts are unpopulated as dedicated slots. Both concepts are nevertheless documented: missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy states 'A missingness table is generated as part of the audit protocol and is included with the dataset; no imputation is applied', and ethical_reviews records an ethics working group memorandum setting out the justification for controlled access to raw voice samples, which functions as a data protection impact analysis.
recommendation: Add an explicit imputation_protocols entry recording that no imputation was applied, and a data_protection_impacts entry pointing to the ethics working group memorandum.

description: source_caveats records five divergent renderings of the award identifier, one of which ('3Tf-OTOD03272001S2', from the documentation footer) does not match any NIH award pattern. The identifiers actually carried in funders.grants - OT2OD032720 and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 - are both well-formed NIH awards, so the malformed variant is quarantined in the caveat rather than propagated into the structured field.
recommendation: No change required to funders.grants; optionally annotate the caveat to mark the footer rendering as a transcription error in the source.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi (doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42) differs from the record's own doi (10.13026/8xbn-nq66). This is correct by design - a version-agnostic resolver alongside a version-specific identifier - and source_caveats states the referent explicitly, but the two DOIs in adjacent fields invite conflation by a reader who does not reach the caveat.
recommendation: Label latest_version_doi inline as the version-agnostic resolver to make the distinction legible at the point of use.

description: collection_timeframes states a 12-month collection period while the IRB protocol in the same source bundle describes a four-year phased study, with pilot collection begun November 2023 and ongoing November 2024. The record flags the tension itself in source_caveats and states which source it preferred and why, so the discrepancy is disclosed rather than concealed, but it remains unresolved.
recommendation: Where possible, state the released dataset's collection window as an explicit date range rather than a duration, and relate it to the wider study period.

description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). It falls below the five-keyword expectation and, more importantly, covers only the domain: none of the disease cohorts (voice, neurological, mood/psychiatric, respiratory disorders), none of the acoustic methods (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory coding, phonetic posteriorgram) and none of the data modalities documented at length elsewhere in the record are reachable by keyword search.
recommendation: Expand keywords with the cohort conditions, the acoustic feature families, the collection modality (speech, cough, breathing) and the platform/standard terms (PhysioNet, BIDS) that already appear in description, instances and preprocessing_strategies.

description: No download_url slot is populated. Access is nevertheless operationally resolvable: the PhysioNet version-specific landing page, the registered-access procedure, the DACO review route and the Synapse controlled-access URLs are all given.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the PhysioNet files endpoint for v3.1.0 so machine clients can resolve the distribution without parsing prose.

description: distribution_formats names formats and even individual file names but records no media_type (MIME) and no character encoding for the TSV and JSON products.
recommendation: Add media_type (application/vnd.apache.parquet, text/tab-separated-values, application/json) and state UTF-8 encoding for the text products.

description: data_protection_impacts states plainly that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk concedes that voice is inherently identifying and that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved. A formal DPIA is the instrument that would normally be expected given that admitted residual risk, even though the consortium substitutes an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access.
recommendation: Conduct and record a formal data protection impact assessment covering the feature-only release, or state explicitly why the published ethical-justification memorandum is held to discharge that function.

description: sensitive_elements declares sensitive_elements_present: true for race/ethnic origin, sexual orientation and socioeconomic/health information, while the notes on the same block state that fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary were removed before release along with household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences. A reader cannot determine from these two statements which sensitive attributes survive into the published feature-only release.
recommendation: Separate the attributes present in the published release from those removed during de-identification, ideally by scoping each sensitive_elements entry to the release it describes.

description: The RRID quoted in citation, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed but identifies PhysioNet as a resource rather than this dataset. It is therefore a platform identifier carried into the citation string, not a persistent identifier for the Bridge2AI-Voice release; the identification burden is carried entirely by the DOI.
recommendation: Retain the DOI as the dataset identifier and label the PhysioNet RRID as a platform resource identifier to avoid the impression that the dataset itself carries an RRID.

description: is_tabular is not set although the release distributes tab-separated phenotype tables, static features and audio quality metrics alongside the Parquet tensors, and the variables block enumerates tabular columns.
recommendation: Set is_tabular to reflect the mixed tabular/array composition of the release, or state the mixture explicitly.

description: No structured imputation_protocols block is present. The substance is supplied instead by missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy, which states that no imputation is performed and that a missingness table accompanies the release, so the concept is documented even though the dedicated slot is empty.
recommendation: Record the no-imputation decision in a structured imputation_protocols entry so it is machine-discoverable.

description: keywords contains only four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai), below the five-term threshold, and covers domain and program affiliation only. No methods terms (machine learning, acoustic features, spectrogram, speech), no condition terms (Parkinson's disease, dysphonia, depression, chronic cough) and no modality terms appear, despite all being described at length elsewhere in the record.
recommendation: Expand keywords to include condition names from the subsets (laryngeal cancer, ALS, Parkinson's disease, depression, airway stenosis), method terms (acoustic biomarkers, audiomics, machine learning, MFCC, spectrogram) and modality terms (speech, cough, respiratory sound).

description: No variables field is present. The record documents that every released table is paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name, and names the tables, but supplies no variable-level identifiers, types or descriptions in the datasheet itself. A reuser must fetch the release to learn what any column means.
recommendation: Add a variables block carrying at least the key linking variables (participant_id, session_id) and the principal phenotype and feature columns with identifiers, types and descriptions, or link each file_collection entry to its specific published data dictionary URL.

description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is false, while the subsets enumerate participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease, other dementias, schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and alcohol or substance use disorder. These are conventionally treated as populations with potentially impaired decisional capacity. The special_protections text partially reconciles the flag by recording that enrollment required the ability to provide informed consent for oneself in English, but the boolean as stated understates the cohort composition.
recommendation: Set at_risk_groups_included to true and describe the capacity-assessment and consent safeguards used for the cognitive-impairment and psychiatric cohorts, rather than resolving the question with a false flag qualified in prose.

description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, while participant_privacy.reidentification_risk and is_deidentified.deidentification_details both state that k-anonymization with k greater than or equal to two is not achieved for the released tables. HIPAA Safe Harbor does not require k-anonymity, so the two claims are reconcilable under that framing, but an unqualified false flag sits awkwardly beside an explicit statement of residual re-identification risk in the released files.
recommendation: Qualify identifiable_elements_present with the standard under which it holds (no HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers) and state the residual quasi-identifier risk alongside it.

description: updates.frequency states a semi-annual cadence, while the release dates recorded in version_access and distribution_dates run January 2025, April 2025, August 2025, December 2025 and May 2026 - approximately quarterly through 2025. The record discloses this discrepancy itself in updates.source_caveats and attributes the semi-annual figure to the project documentation.
recommendation: State the observed cadence as the operative one and retain the documented semi-annual commitment as the stated policy, distinguishing the two.

description: data_protection_impacts.impact_details describes an ethicist review of sensitive fields and a published memorandum justifying controlled access, while its source_caveats records that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether an impact analysis on data subjects was conducted. The tension is disclosed rather than concealed, and the substantive activities described do constitute an impact assessment in effect.
recommendation: State explicitly whether a formal DPIA instrument was completed, distinguishing it from the ethics review of sensitive fields that is described.

description: No download_url field is populated. The platform link is nonetheless available: distribution_formats[].access_urls give the versioned PhysioNet URL and the Synapse controlled-access URL, page resolves to the same PhysioNet record, and data_governance.access_review_process gives step-by-step access instructions for both tiers.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the versioned PhysioNet files URL so that automated harvesters find the access point in the canonical slot.

description: is_tabular is not set, although the release is substantially tabular (TSV phenotype tables and static features, Parquet feature tables with a documented row granularity of one row per unique recording).
recommendation: Set is_tabular to true for the phenotype and static feature components, or qualify it per file_collection given the mixed dense-array and tabular content.

description: The RRID cited in the citation string, RRID:SCR_007345, is well formed but identifies PhysioNet as a resource rather than this dataset. The citation therefore carries a repository RRID, not a dataset-level persistent identifier; the dataset-level identification rests on the DOI, which is valid.
recommendation: Label the RRID explicitly as the hosting repository's identifier to avoid it being read as a dataset RRID.

description: funders.notes records two award strings from the project documentation, 3TF-OT2ActfOD032720Projectf01S1 and 3Tf-OTOD03272001S2, that do not match any NIH award pattern. The record identifies them as corrupted renderings of the same core award rather than presenting them as valid identifiers, which is the correct handling; the primary awards cited are well formed.
recommendation: No change required; the corruption is already labelled. Optionally drop the corrupted strings and retain only the note that the source text was garbled.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, an identifier that appears nowhere else in the record and that conflicts with the record's own DOI for the latest listed version (3.1.0 = doi:10.13026/8xbn-nq66, listed in versions_available and in doi/id/citation).
recommendation: Correct latest_version_doi to 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, or state explicitly which release 10.13026/37yb-1t42 designates if a newer version exists.

description: Unreconciled HIPAA characterization: regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant is 'compliant' and other_compliance states HIPAA de-identification rules were applied, while regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats records that the Data Transfer and Use Agreement calls the transferred data personally identifiable information 'not covered under HIPAA, FERPA, or similar laws'. The record flags the conflict but leaves a downstream user unable to determine the operative regime for the raw-audio transfer.
recommendation: State which regime governs which tier (registered-access features vs controlled-access raw audio) rather than recording both characterizations side by side.

description: keywords contains only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). No method terms (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory features, speech), no condition terms (Parkinson's disease, dysphonia, depression, COPD) and no modality terms, although all of these are described at length elsewhere in the record.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering domain, modality, methods and represented conditions so that the record is discoverable by condition and by feature type.

description: data_protection_impacts states that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted, for a dataset that the record itself classifies as containing race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic, mental-health and clinical-diagnosis data derived from a biometric signal. The absence is honestly reported, but it is a substantive governance gap rather than a documentation gap.
recommendation: Conduct and document a data protection impact assessment covering the released feature tiers, or record why the IRB review and ethicist-led sensitive-field removal are held to serve that function.

description: is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false while the same block states that 'K-anonymization with k of two or more is not achieved' and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that voice cannot be fully de-identified. The claims are reconcilable for this release (raw audio is withheld and direct identifiers removed), but the boolean reads more absolutely than the surrounding prose.
recommendation: Qualify the boolean in deidentification_details to distinguish direct identifiers (removed) from quasi-identifier combinations (not k-anonymized).

description: The participant count of 833 is attributed to version 3.1.0 in description and instances.counts, while source_caveats records that the figure comes from documentation written against version 3.0, and related_datasets notes that 3.0.0 itself added 391 participants over 2.0.1. The record discloses the provenance of the figure but still asserts it for 3.1.0.
recommendation: Either cite the count as the version 3.0 figure carried forward, or give the 3.1.0 participant total from the release itself.

description: No data-standard conformance is asserted for this release: conforms_to is absent and conforms_to_schema names the metadata record's own schema (w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) rather than a standard the data conforms to. source_caveats explains that earlier releases were converted to BIDS v1.9.0 but that the 3.1.0 features/metadata/phenotype layout states no such conformance.
recommendation: State whether the 3.1.0 layout still conforms to BIDS v1.9.0 or to any feature-file convention, since interoperability of the Parquet feature tensors otherwise depends entirely on the per-file JSON dictionaries.

description: Several schema slots that the rubric reads are unused even though equivalent content exists elsewhere: download_url (access URLs appear only inside distribution_formats and data_governance.access_review_process), is_tabular, character encoding on any distributed file, Parquet media_type, imputation_protocols, and data_governance.committee_contact (the DACO mailbox appears only in notes).
recommendation: Populate the dedicated slots so machine consumers reach the same facts the prose carries; record explicitly that no imputation was performed if that is the case.

description: maintainers records NIH under role 'government_agency' with maintainer_details describing award support. That is funding provenance rather than maintenance of the released artifact, and it duplicates funders.
recommendation: Reserve maintainers for parties that operate or curate the release (PhysioNet, the consortium, DACO) and leave award support to funders.

description: variables enumerates only four fields (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of diagnosis and questionnaire tables. Column-level semantics are delegated to the per-file JSON data dictionaries, which are described but not enumerated in the record.
recommendation: Either extend variables to cover the principal phenotype and static-feature columns or link the data dictionaries individually.

description: updates.frequency states a semi-annual (twice yearly) cadence, but the release history the record itself supplies is denser and irregular: 2025-01-17 (1.1), 2025-04-16 (2.0.0), 2025-08-18 (2.0.1), 2025-12-16 (3.0.0), 2026-05-01 (3.1.0) — five releases in roughly sixteen months. The record caveats that the cadence statement was written against Health Data Nexus hosting, but does not reconcile it with the observed PhysioNet release pattern.
recommendation: Restate the update cadence against the PhysioNet release history, or mark the semi-annual figure as a planning target rather than an observed frequency.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is given as doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which related_datasets (relationship_type: is_version_of) identifies as the concept DOI resolving to the latest version. The DOI of the version actually described by this record is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. A field named latest_version_doi holding a concept DOI is a slot/value mismatch that could mislead an automated consumer.
recommendation: Either record the resolved version DOI (10.13026/8xbn-nq66) in latest_version_doi, or rename/annotate the value explicitly as the concept DOI.

description: keywords contains only four broad terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice). No clinical condition (Parkinson's disease, ALS, laryngeal cancer, depression), no modality or method term (spectrogram, MFCC, acoustic features, speech), and no data-type term appears, despite all of these being prominent in the description and phenotype inventory. Searchability is materially weaker than the rest of the record would support.
recommendation: Extend keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering conditions, acoustic feature types, and study design, drawn from content already present in description and file_collections.

description: The dedicated download_url slot is unpopulated. Platform access is nonetheless locatable: distribution_formats.access_urls give https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ for both formats, raw_sources.access_url gives the Synapse controlled-access location, and license_and_use_terms states the credentialing steps.
recommendation: Populate download_url with the PhysioNet content URL so machine consumers do not have to reach into distribution_formats.

description: at_risk_populations is not used; the vulnerable-population content lives in human_subject_research.special_populations (neurological/neurodegenerative cohorts including mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's, ALS, Parkinson's; mood and psychiatric cohorts including depression, bipolar, PTSD). The information is present and specific, but in a non-canonical slot.
recommendation: Mirror the special_populations content into at_risk_populations with the protections applied to each group.

description: content_warnings.content_warnings_present is false while a warnings entry is supplied. The record explains the pairing (the warning describes free-speech transcripts removed at 1.1 and excluded from the feature-only 3.0.0/3.1.0 releases), so the semantics are recoverable, but the boolean and the populated list read as contradictory to a consumer that reads only the flag.
recommendation: Move the superseded warning into a historical-notes field, or set the flag to reflect that a caveat text is carried.

description: confidential_elements_present is false while sensitive_elements_present is true, access is credentialed/restricted, a Certificate of Confidentiality applies, and the Data Transfer and Use Agreement characterizes the data as personally identifiable information under OMB M-07-16. The record flags the tension in source_caveats and scopes the false answer to the feature-only release, which makes the position defensible but not self-evidently coherent.
recommendation: State explicitly in confidentiality_details why doctor-patient-privileged content is absent from a release that is nonetheless credentialed and covered by a Certificate of Confidentiality.

description: sensitive_elements carries an acknowledged internal conflict: the healthsheet inventory lists race, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information as present, while the version 3.0.0 de-identification account states that all REDCap-flagged sensitive fields and highly sensitive non-identifying elements (household income, mental health status, traumatic life experiences) were removed. The record reports both rather than resolving which holds for 3.1.0.
recommendation: Resolve against the 3.1.0 file inventory: enumerate which sensitive attributes are actually present in the released phenotype tables.

description: variables enumerates only four elements (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release whose phenotype directory holds dozens of tables across confounders, demographics, eighteen diagnosis tables, enrollment and thirteen questionnaires. The record compensates by documenting that every table ships a companion JSON data dictionary carrying description, question text and data type.
recommendation: Either expand variables to cover the principal analytic columns, or add an explicit pointer field stating that the authoritative variable metadata is the distributed JSON data dictionaries.

description: conforms_to is deliberately omitted, with source_caveats explaining that the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion describes the audio dataset's folder layout rather than this feature-only release. The omission is honest, but it leaves no data-level community-standard conformance assertion for the released artifact; ICD-10 appears only as a labeling protocol and conforms_to_schema describes the datasheet, not the data.
recommendation: State any standard the released tables do follow (for example the phenotype/JSON data-dictionary convention, ICD-10 coding of diagnosis columns) in conforms_to, scoped to this release.

description: The RRID carried in the citation string (RRID:SCR_007345) is the resource identifier of PhysioNet, the hosting platform, not of the Bridge2AI-Voice dataset. The format is valid and the usage follows PhysioNet's own citation convention, but the identifier does not uniquely identify this dataset.
recommendation: Keep the platform RRID in the citation but note that dataset-level identification rests on the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66.

description: collection_timeframes supplies no start or end dates. The twelve-month figure is caveated as drawn from documentation written against versions 2.0.0/3.0.0, and the record itself observes that the cohort accumulated across releases from 306 to 833 participants, so the stated span probably does not describe the assembly of the released cohort.
recommendation: Record first and last collection dates for the 3.1.0 cohort, or state that they are unavailable from any source.

description: Only four keywords are supplied (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice), below the five-keyword threshold, and all four are generic. None names a disease cohort (Parkinson's, ALS, dysphonia, COPD, depression), a modality term (speech, cough, breath, spectrogram, MFCC), a method term (machine learning, acoustic features, audiomics) or the hosting platform. A dataset spanning four clinical cohorts is under-indexed for discovery by exactly the terms a searcher would use.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least 8-12 terms covering the four disorder cohorts, the acoustic modalities and feature families, audiomics, and PhysioNet.

description: No data_protection_impacts entry is present although the release carries health, mental-health, race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation derived data and the record itself assesses residual re-identification risk. The absence is disclosed rather than silent: source_caveats states 'the project documentation states that no analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted'. The disclosure is good practice, but the DPIA limb of Element 4 sub-element 1 remains substantively unmet.
recommendation: Conduct and record a data protection impact assessment covering the derived-feature release, given the acknowledged inherent identifiability of voice-derived signals.

description: conforms_to is deliberately not asserted for this release, so no community data standard is claimed for the distributed features and phenotype tables. source_caveats explains that BIDS 1.9.0 conformance belongs to the controlled-access raw audio distribution rather than to the PhysioNet featurized release, and records the BIDS fact against related_datasets instead. conforms_to_schema is populated but points at the datasheet's own metadata schema (w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema), which does not help a consumer harmonize the data.
recommendation: State any content-level standard the featurized release does satisfy, or record an explicit negative conformance statement in conforms_to so the absence is machine-readable rather than confined to prose caveats.

description: The variables list contains four entries (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) against a release holding hundreds of phenotype columns across 18 diagnosis tables and 13 questionnaire instruments, plus per-feature columns in static_features.tsv. The four documented variables are the cross-file join keys and are documented well, and file_collections states that every table is paired with a JSON data dictionary giving per-column descriptions, question text and data type, so the mechanism for full coverage is disclosed; the datasheet itself nevertheless exposes almost none of it.
recommendation: Either lift a representative subset of phenotype and static-feature variables into variables, or cite the resolvable location of each JSON data dictionary so variable metadata is reachable from the datasheet.

description: No conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the record, although Element 9 sub-element 5 asks for one alongside ethical review. The consortium spans fifteen named lead investigators across twelve institutions and an NIH award, which is the circumstance in which such a statement is normally expected.
recommendation: Add a conflicts-of-interest declaration for the investigator group to the ethical_reviews block.

description: at_risk_populations declines to determine whether the neurological cohort (which includes mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, where capacity to consent may be impaired) or the mood and psychiatric cohort are at-risk groups, recording in source_caveats that 'the bundle makes no statement ... so no determination is recorded here'. The IRB protocol is reported as identifying only children under that heading. Declining to infer beyond the source is methodologically correct for the datasheet, but it leaves an unresolved protection question for cohorts the dataset demonstrably contains.
recommendation: Obtain and record the protocol's position on capacity assessment and surrogate or assented consent for the cognitive-impairment cohort.

description: Three declared schema slots that the rubric names as evidence paths are unpopulated, with the substance carried elsewhere: download_url is empty (access URLs appear under distribution_formats.access_urls and data_governance.access_review_process); is_tabular is absent although the phenotype and static-feature tables are plainly tabular; character encoding is not stated for any distributed file.
recommendation: Populate download_url, set is_tabular, and declare the character encoding of the tab-delimited tables and JSON dictionaries.

description: Ontology references are given as bare CURIEs without labels or resolvable prefixes: instances carry data_topic: B2AI_TOPIC:36 and data_substrate: B2AI_SUBSTRATE:69. A reader cannot determine what topic or substrate is meant from the datasheet alone, even though the same concepts are described richly in prose elsewhere in the record.
recommendation: Accompany each CURIE with its human-readable label and register the B2AI_TOPIC and B2AI_SUBSTRATE prefixes against a resolvable namespace.

description: Several genuine source conflicts exist but are surfaced and adjudicated rather than concealed, which is the correct handling and is recorded here as a positive consistency finding rather than a defect: award identifiers differ across sources (PhysioNet 3OT2OD032720-01S1, RePORTER 3OT2OD032720-01S3, publication 1OT2OD032720-01, and a garbled documentation footer), with the stable core project number OT2OD032720 identified; the healthsheet answer 'No, they are unrelated' on instance relationships is recorded beside the release notes describing repeated sessions per participant; and the ~61,937 recording figure for version 3.0 is set beside the 28,640-32,522 per-feature counts for 3.1.0 with no false reconciliation attempted.
recommendation: No change required; retain this caveat discipline in future releases.

description: Subpopulation characterization is qualitative only. subpopulations.identification names the dimensions collected (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and distribution describes the skew and its causes, but no counts or percentages are given for any demographic stratum, nor per-cohort participant counts against the 833 total. A user assessing fitness for a fairness study cannot size any subgroup from the datasheet.
recommendation: Add per-cohort and per-demographic-stratum counts, which the phenotype demographics tables already support.

description: version_access.latest_version_doi is doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which differs from this record's doi of 10.13026/8xbn-nq66. This is not an error: version_details explains that 10.13026/37yb-1t42 is the resolver DOI for the latest version while 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 pins version 3.1.0. The field name alone could nonetheless be read as contradicting the record's own identifier.
recommendation: Rename or annotate the slot to make clear it holds a concept-level resolver DOI rather than the DOI of the version described.

description: Internal contradiction in the de-identification account. is_deidentified.method records the de-identification type as "NoDeIdentification" with the explanation that "no identifiers were collected, so no active de-identification was necessary", yet participant_privacy.anonymization_method states that "Protected Health Information as defined by the HIPAA Privacy Rule was removed from the public release via the Safe Harbor method", is_deidentified.identifiers_removed enumerates removed PHI, sex, race/ethnicity and medications, and human_subject_research.regulatory_compliance states "The public release is de-identified under the HIPAA Privacy Rule Safe Harbor method". Removal by Safe Harbor is an active de-identification operation, so the two accounts cannot both hold. Unlike the six conflicts the record resolves in source_caveats, this one carries no caveat and is presented as settled fact.
recommendation: Reconcile the two statements or add a source_caveats note under is_deidentified stating that the dataset_description enum value "NoDeIdentification" conflicts with the Safe Harbor removal described in the healthsheet and licence material, and state which governs the released artifact.

description: Human-subjects / data-protection gate: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is true and the release carries retinal imaging, continuous glucose, wearable and cognitive-test data, but data_protection_impacts is absent as a field. The notes disclose that "no data protection impact analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted". The absence is honestly disclosed rather than concealed, but the artifact itself is missing, which is what Q8's 5-point band requires.
recommendation: Conduct and record a DPIA covering the AI/ML re-identification pathway the record already identifies under participant_privacy.reidentification_risk, and populate data_protection_impacts rather than only noting the gap in free-text notes.

description: Sustainability claim is undercut by the record's own facts. version_access lists "2.0.0 — DOI 10.60775/fairhub.2 ... no longer accessible" and records that "older versions will not continue to be supported"; related_datasets nevertheless links doi:10.60775/fairhub.2 as an is_new_version_of target. A registered DOI that no longer resolves to accessible content is a persistence failure, not merely a version retirement. The notes add that the FAIRhub landing pages carry the notice "This repository is under review for potential modification in compliance with Administration directives" and that the platform is "currently in beta".
recommendation: State the preservation commitment for retired versions explicitly (tombstone page, metadata-only DOI landing page, or archival copy) so that superseded DOIs remain resolvable, and record the institutional preservation commitment that survives the current platform-review notice.

description: sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present is false and confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, while participant_privacy simultaneously records "a theoretical risk of future re-identification", notes that "AI algorithms can infer individual patient characteristics and could facilitate individual-level identification", and documents watermarking, a strict licence and a robust dissemination system as deterrents. Declaring no sensitive elements while deploying anti-re-identification controls over retinal images, ten-day CGM traces and wrist-worn activity records is internally uneasy, even though the record correctly attributes the "No" answers to the healthsheet.
recommendation: Qualify the sensitive_elements answer to distinguish "contains no direct identifiers or controlled-access attributes" from "contains no data of a sensitive character", since dense biometric time series are ordinarily treated as the latter.

description: Licence scope tension. license_and_use_terms.license_terms grants use "for research, commercial and non-commercial purposes", while license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission is disease_specific_research and intended_uses.usage_notes states "The public version of the dataset may only be used for type 2 diabetes related research". The two are reconcilable only by reading the grant as permitting commercial T2DM research; the record does not say so.
recommendation: Add one clause clarifying that the commercial grant is bounded by the disease-specific attestation, so a reader does not infer an unrestricted commercial licence from the licence summary.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is recorded as "restricted", which is more restrictive than either underlying source: the RO-Crate gives confidentialityLevel "HL7:2N (normal)" and the FAIRhub dataset description gives accessType "PublicDownloadSelfAttestationRequired". The record flags the mapping transparently in regulatory_restrictions.source_caveats, so this is a disclosed enum-mapping approximation rather than a hidden error, but a downstream consumer reading only the enum will overstate the access tier.
recommendation: Retain the caveat and, if the schema permits, carry the verbatim source values alongside the mapped enum so the approximation travels with the value.

description: distribution_formats declares four formats (DICOM, CSV, JSON, Markdown) but does not list WFDB, which file_collections.cardiac_ecg records as the format of all 4,515 ECG files, and folds the .tsv metadata files (manifest.tsv, participants.tsv) under the CSV entry with media_type text/csv rather than text/tab-separated-values. The format inventory is therefore narrower and slightly less precise than the file_collections it summarises.
recommendation: Add a WFDB entry to distribution_formats and separate TSV from CSV with media_type text/tab-separated-values.
