description: No demographic characterization appears anywhere — no age, sex, race, ethnicity or geographic distribution, and no per-subpopulation counts. This is in direct tension with stated purposes ('the most diverse, high-resolution, ethically sourced, AI-ready data set'), the title's 'for Equitable AI', and the 'social determinants of health' keyword. Without demographics no fairness analysis of the released cohort is possible, which is also why known_biases cannot be substantiated.
recommendation: Add demographic composition of the released 50,000 admissions with counts per ICU/PICU/NICU subpopulation, enabling the equity claims and a fairness assessment to be verified.

description: prohibited_uses and discouraged_uses are both absent for a controlled-access dataset of critically ill patients' PHI. intended_uses is developed in detail across three categories, so the use guidance is one-sided: no prohibition on re-identification attempts, redistribution, or clinical deployment of unvalidated models is recorded, even though such terms are presumably in the signed licensing agreement.
recommendation: Surface the prohibitions from the licensing agreement into prohibited_uses (notably re-identification and redistribution) and add discouraged_uses for analyses the cohort cannot support.

description: No version identifier, version_access or errata exist for a dataset that is explicitly and actively growing (updates describes expansion toward 100,000 admissions across 9 modalities, with imaging and EEG still arriving). Users cannot name which state of a moving dataset they analysed, and the maintainers entry notes a package status page listing versions for software while the dataset itself carries none.
recommendation: Assign a dataset version or dated snapshot identifier to each released state and record version_access, so analyses over a growing enclave dataset remain reproducible.

description: No common identifier for cross-modality linkage is documented. The datasheet describes nine modality subsets held in different places (OMOP and telemetry in the enclave, notes local to sites, imaging and EEG partly pending) but never states the key on which an admission's OMOP rows, waveforms, images and note tokens are joined — the central integration question for a multimodal AI-ready dataset.
recommendation: Document the person/admission identifier used to link modalities (e.g. OMOP person_id and visit_occurrence_id) and the procedure for joining waveform, imaging and note-token artifacts to it.

description: The external resource 'CHoRUS page on the Bridge2AI website' is recorded as 'www.bridge2ai.org/chorus' without a URI scheme, unlike the other two external resources which are well-formed https URIs. As written it is not a resolvable URI value.
recommendation: Record the value as https://www.bridge2ai.org/chorus.

description: The maintainer contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains a misspelled domain ('havard' for 'harvard'). The record transcribes the published value faithfully and flags the error in source_caveats, which is the right provenance behaviour, but the listed maintainer contact is not usable as given.
recommendation: Retain the transcription caveat but add a corrected, verified contact address so the maintainer is reachable.

description: collection_timeframes is populated but gives no clinical date range: it states retrospective collection reflecting a state 'as of August 2025' without the admission years covered. A critical care cohort whose temporal span is unknown cannot be assessed for practice drift, COVID-era effects, or comparability with other ICU datasets.
recommendation: State the earliest and latest admission dates represented in the released extract, separately from the extraction/as-of date.

description: sampling_strategies.is_sample=true and describes an intent to ensure a balanced, diverse cohort, but its own source_caveats concedes that the executed sampling frame, inclusion criteria and any verification of representativeness are undocumented. Stated intent is therefore not evidence of the released cohort's composition, and the same gap weakens the selection-bias mitigation claim in known_biases.
recommendation: Document the executed inclusion/exclusion criteria and per-site contribution counts for the released cohort, distinguishing them from the project's sampling aspirations.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects=true for a 50,000-admission clinical EHR dataset, but ethical_reviews names no institutional review board, ethics committee or reviewing organization and states no approval number. The two ethical_reviews entries describe community ethics focus groups and community-perspective research, which are project ethics activities rather than regulatory review of the dataset. The record itself discloses this gap in human_subject_research.source_caveats ('The bundle does not name an IRB or ethics review board, nor state an approval number, for the dataset.'), which is honest but does not supply the missing governance evidence.
recommendation: Add an ethical_reviews entry naming the reviewing IRB (for a multi-site consortium, the single IRB of record), its institution and the protocol/approval number governing the retrospective extraction and the enclave.

description: involves_human_subjects=true but there is no informed_consent field at all. For a retrospective EHR/PACS/telemetry dataset the expected documentation is a waiver of informed consent or HIPAA authorization waiver under 45 CFR 46.116(f) / 45 CFR 164.512(i); neither the waiver nor any consent pathway is recorded, and the record does not mark the absence at this location.
recommendation: Add informed_consent documenting the consent basis - most likely an IRB-approved waiver of consent and of HIPAA authorization for retrospective secondary use - or state explicitly that no waiver determination is available in the sources.

description: is_deidentified is populated with a method, but no de-identification standard is named (neither HIPAA Safe Harbor nor Expert Determination), no identifiers removed are enumerated, and participant_privacy.reidentification_risk is absent. The stated method - 'approaches that limit re-identification' - is a paraphrase rather than a specification, and imaging de-identification was still 'in process'. The record further notes that privacy_scan_tool and CTP-deid exist in the GitHub organization but does not state that either was applied to the released data, so no tool-to-artifact link closes the loop.
recommendation: Name the de-identification standard applied per modality, enumerate the identifier classes removed or shifted (dates, geography, device identifiers), state residual re-identification risk, and link the CTP-deid / privacy_scan_tool pipelines to the modalities they were actually run against.

description: Deidentification-method appropriateness cannot be confirmed against the data type. The dataset carries high-risk quasi-identifiers - nursing flowsheets at high frequency, second-resolution waveform telemetry, EEG, DICOM pixel and header data, and DeGauss-geocoded OMOP Location entities - yet the documented protections are tokenization of note text plus controlled enclave access. Geocoding in particular increases rather than reduces re-identification risk and is listed under preprocessing_strategies with no corresponding protection in participant_privacy.
recommendation: State how geocoded location, DICOM headers and high-frequency waveform timestamps are protected (e.g. geographic generalization, date shifting, header scrubbing) so the method can be judged appropriate to each substrate.

description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included=true, with PICU and NICU minors identified in human_subject_research.special_populations and subpopulations, but no assent procedures, guardian permission procedures or additional safeguards are described. The record discloses this in at_risk_populations.source_caveats rather than documenting the protections.
recommendation: Document the subpart D determination for pediatric and neonatal records and any parental permission or waiver relied upon.

description: The dataset is US hospital PHI held under restricted confidentiality, yet regulatory_restrictions records no HIPAA determination, no limited-data-set/DUA characterization and no other_compliance entry. The record notes HIPAA and GDPR appear only as topics of a training workshop. A restricted clinical dataset with no stated regulatory basis leaves the access terms semantically incomplete.
recommendation: State the HIPAA status of the released data (de-identified data set, limited data set under a DUA, or PHI under authorization/waiver) and record it in regulatory_restrictions.

description: No DOI or other persistent identifier is present anywhere in the record. The id field is 'https://chorus4ai.org/', which is identical to the page field: a project homepage, not a persistent identifier, and not a dataset-level landing page. Findability and sustainability therefore rest entirely on a resolvable but non-persistent project URL, against a dataset the record simultaneously describes as released and third-party shared.
recommendation: Mint a dataset DOI (DataCite via the hosting institution or a domain repository) and set id to the DOI rather than reusing the project homepage URL.

description: distribution_formats enumerates five formats as if the dataset were distributed, while regulatory_restrictions states that 'Data are worked with inside a cloud enclave rather than distributed as files' and confidential_elements states the dataset 'is not openly downloadable'. The formats are therefore in-enclave working formats, not distribution formats, and no download_url exists. A reader taking distribution_formats at face value would form an incorrect expectation of how the data are obtained.
recommendation: Relabel these as in-enclave data formats, or add a note to distribution_formats clarifying that access is analysis-in-place within the Collaborative Cloud and that no file distribution occurs.

description: license_and_use_terms describes only a licensing agreement embedded in the AIM-AHEAD training-program registration form, and its source_caveats confirm no data use license is named for the dataset itself. Meanwhile third_party_sharing.is_shared=true and data_governance.access_review_process describes a general route via two email contacts. The consequence is that the terms governing the non-training-program access route are undocumented, so 'shared' and 'licensed' are not reconciled.
recommendation: Name and link the data use agreement that governs general access, distinct from the training-program registration licence, and state whether the MIT/Apache-2.0 software licences carry any implication for derived data artifacts.

description: Two unreconciled volume disagreements propagate into the scored composition fields. Admissions: 50,000 (project website) versus 'over 45K unique admissions' (September 2025 webinar). Imaging: 7,642 admissions with radiology data (website) versus approximately 1,000 images available with de-identification in process (webinar). The record discloses both at description, instances.source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats and applies a stated source-ranking rule, which is good practice, but the headline instances.counts values (50000, 7642) are presented without inline qualification and are the values a downstream consumer will read.
recommendation: Carry the disagreement into the counts themselves (e.g. a range or an as-of date qualifier on each count) so the reconciliation is visible without reading source_caveats.

description: instances.counts for OMOP rows is given as the exact integer 1600000000, which the record's own note identifies as its expansion of the rounded website figure '1.6 Billion Rows of EHR OMOP data' and 'not a count reported exactly by any source'. The disclosure is exemplary, but the serialized value implies ten significant figures of precision the source does not support.
recommendation: Record rounded magnitudes as approximate (e.g. a count_approximate flag or an order-of-magnitude field) rather than as an exact integer.

description: There is no known_biases field, despite a title that reads 'Patient-Focused Collaborative Hospital Repository Uniting Standards (CHoRUS) for Equitable AI', keywords including 'social determinants of health', and a stated purpose of building AI models for clinical deployment. Relevant bias-adjacent content exists but sits in known_limitations (representativeness_limitation) and in a single clause of future_use_impacts about managing 'privacy and bias'; no bias is categorized, no taxonomy (BiasTypeEnum / AIO) is referenced, and no fairness analysis across the ICU/PICU/NICU or demographic strata is reported.
recommendation: Populate known_biases with typed entries - selection bias from 14 academic critical-care centers, measurement bias across heterogeneous site EHR instrumentation and monitor vendors, differential missingness across modalities - mapped to a standard taxonomy, and add a fairness analysis across the documented subpopulations.

description: No version, version_access or errata field exists, and no persistent identifier anchors any release. The record describes a moving target (50,000 admissions now, 100,000 anticipated; imaging and EEG still in process; metadata for three of nine modalities 'planned') with no way to cite the state a given analysis used. updates.source_caveats confirms no update frequency or versioning policy. Sustainability is further exposed by the award period ending 2026-11-30 with no stated preservation commitment beyond it, and by the site banner recorded in notes.
recommendation: Introduce dated, citable releases with version identifiers and per-version DOIs, publish a versioning and errata policy, and state the preservation commitment and hosting arrangement beyond the OT2OD032701 project period.

description: The maintainer contact address 'cmccrary@mgh.havard.edu' contains an apparent misspelling of the harvard.edu domain. The record marks it 'address as printed on the site', so the transcription is faithful to the source rather than introduced here, but the contact as recorded is likely unroutable - which matters because this is the named project contact.
recommendation: Verify the address against an independent source and record the corrected form with a note that the website copy contains a typo.

description: One external resource URL is recorded without a scheme ('www.bridge2ai.org/chorus') and is embedded in prose alongside 'AIM-AHEAD.net', while the remaining URLs (https://chorus4ai.org/, https://github.com/chorus-ai, https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema) are well formed and use plausible domains. Several external_resources entries name repositories (Chorus_SOP, chorus-mapping, chorus_waveform, chorus-extract-upload, privacy_scan_tool, CTP-deid, UF-Geocoding, CHoRUSReports) without individual URLs, so they are not directly resolvable.
recommendation: Give each named repository its own absolute https URL rather than relying on the organization-level link plus a repository name in prose.

description: labeling_strategies, splits and parts of tasks describe project intentions in the future tense ('a visualization and annotation environment will label data', 'will also provision a holdout test set') and are recorded in fields whose semantics imply realized dataset properties. The record flags this at labeling_strategies.source_caveats, splits.source_caveats and the top-level source_caveats, so the intent/state distinction is preserved - but a consumer reading splits alone would infer a holdout set exists when its size, composition and availability are unstated.
recommendation: Add an explicit realized/planned status flag on forward-looking entries so the distinction survives field-level extraction.

description: Version ordering is internally inconsistent: this June 2026 release is declared version '2.0', while version_access lists the earlier June 2025 and October 2025 releases at version '2.1'. The citation string additionally identifies the deposit as 'V2'. A later release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors breaks the temporal ordering a consumer would use to select the newest data.
recommendation: Reconcile the release version with the Dataverse deposit version series (e.g., 2.2 or 3.0 for a release superseding 2.1), or state explicitly that the release version and the Dataverse V-number are distinct numbering schemes.

description: preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools document the MuSIC cell-map construction pipeline (node2vec, DenseNet-121 embeddings, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GPT-4/GSAI naming), but known_limitations states that this release 'does not contain predicted cell maps'. The processing actually applied to the released artifacts (mass-spectrometry search and elution-profile processing, immunofluorescence image QC, Perturb-seq alignment and guide assignment) is therefore undocumented.
recommendation: Add preprocessing entries describing how the released SEC-MS, AP-MS, IF image, and Perturb-seq files were produced, and label the MuSIC pipeline entries as downstream analysis of future releases.

description: third_party_sharing and raw_sources assert deposition in MassIVE, the Sequence Read Archive (via an NCBI BioProject), and Figshare, but no accession identifiers or URLs are given for any of these deposits, so the external raw data are named but not resolvable from this record.
recommendation: Record MassIVE accessions (MSV…), the BioProject accession (PRJNA…), and the Figshare DOI for each external deposit.

description: File sizes are recorded only as human-readable strings inside file_collections descriptions ('3.8 GB', '113.3 KB') with total_size_bytes omitted; MD5 checksums are present but no byte counts. The record explains this in source_caveats, but machine-readable size metadata is still absent.
recommendation: Populate file_collections.total_bytes and total_size_bytes with exact byte counts from the Dataverse file API.

description: Temporal fields do not form a single clean ordering: issued 2026-06-17 precedes the 2026-07-15 publication date recorded for the three immunofluorescence file collections; created_on 2025-02-27 is acknowledged in source_caveats as carried unchanged from earlier releases; and updates promise quarterly augmentation 'through the end of the project in November 2026' while the funder record gives a project period ending 2026-08-31.
recommendation: State a dataset-level last_updated_on, and reconcile the stated project end date with the NIH project period or explain the no-cost extension.

description: Three Q1 mandatory-field slots are unpopulated: variables (no variable-level metadata for the released tables), parent_datasets (prior releases are captured only as related_datasets with is_new_version_of), and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level (a confidentiality determination is made narratively in confidential_elements but is not expressed as the schema's classification enum).
recommendation: Add variable metadata for the tabular components of the SEC-MS and Perturb-seq packages and set confidentiality_level explicitly.

description: Ethics contact affiliation mismatch: Vardit Ravitsky is listed in creators with affiliation 'University of Montreal', while the ethical_reviews contact email for the same person is ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org and the description names the Hastings Center as a partner institution.
recommendation: Record both affiliations for the ethics lead, or align the creator affiliation with the institution used for ethics correspondence.

description: human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and no data_protection_impacts or formal reidentification_risk assessment is recorded, yet the record discloses donor-level attributes of the source material (a 51-year-old Black female metastatic breast cancer donor; a healthy male Northern European iPSC donor). The non-human-subjects determination is well supported for de-identified commercial cell lines, but the residual re-identification question for donor-derived genomic material is asserted rather than assessed.
recommendation: Add an explicit reidentification_risk statement for the genomic (Perturb-seq/SRA) components covering donor genotype inference, even where the overall determination remains non-human-subjects.

description: machine_annotation_tools name four tools (node2vec, DenseNet-121, GPT-4, HiDeF) with informative descriptions but no version numbers or per-tool repository URLs; imputation_protocols, missing_data_documentation, annotation_analyses and errata are absent entirely.
recommendation: Pin tool versions (e.g., HiDeF release, GPT-4 model snapshot) and link each tool to its repository; add an errata slot even if empty for this release.

description: Version sequence is non-monotonic across the release series. This release (issued 2026-06-17) carries version '2.0', while the two EARLIER releases it supersedes are recorded at higher version numbers: June 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, 'version 2.1') and October 2025 (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM, 'version 2.1'). The March 2025 release is 'version 1.4'. A consumer ordering releases by version string would place this release before its own predecessors.
recommendation: Reconcile the version numbering across the series (e.g. assign this release a version strictly greater than 2.1), or state explicitly that Dataverse per-dataset version numbers are local to each deposit and are not comparable across releases.

description: The documented preprocessing pipeline does not correspond to the artifacts actually released. preprocessing_strategies and machine_annotation_tools describe cell-map construction (node2vec PPI embedding, DenseNet-121 image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, HiDeF community detection, GSAI/GPT-4 assembly naming), but known_limitations and discouraged_uses state that 'computed cell maps are not included in this release'. No preprocessing is documented for what is released: no mass-spectrometry search or quantification parameters for the AP-MS/SEC-MS packages, no image processing or segmentation for the IF archives, and no alignment/QC pipeline for the Perturb-seq atlas.
recommendation: Add preprocessing_strategies entries for the released modalities (MS search engine and settings, image acquisition/processing, scRNA-seq alignment and QC thresholds) and mark the cell-map pipeline entries as pertaining to a downstream product not contained in this release.

description: Embargo statements conflict with what is distributed. external_resources and third_party_sharing record the Perturb-seq depositions for both KOLF2.1J iPSCs and MDA-MB-468 as embargoed, yet the release distributes cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip. Their stated sizes (30.2 KB and 73.3 KB) are implausibly small for a genome-scale atlas of 11,739 targeted genes or for raw SRA sequence data, suggesting pointer/manifest packages rather than data; the record does not say so. The same question arises for the SEC-MS and AP-MS packages (93.9 KB to 171.8 KB) against multi-GB image archives.
recommendation: State explicitly what each small archive contains (metadata, manifests, accession pointers, or processed matrices) and how the embargo on the external depositions relates to the contents distributed here.

description: No variable-level metadata. The Q1 field set variables, resources and parent_datasets is entirely unpopulated, and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is not asserted. For the tabular outputs (SEC-MS elution profiles, AP-MS interaction tables, Perturb-seq atlas) the absence of VariableMetadata leaves column semantics, units and value ranges undocumented, which is the semantic/statistical characterization axis of the Bridge2AI AI-readiness criteria the record itself invokes.
recommendation: Add variables entries for the tabular distributions and assign a confidentiality_level classification consistent with the CC BY-NC-SA release and the documented embargoes.

description: File sizes are not machine-readable. total_size_bytes is omitted at dataset level and total_bytes is omitted on all ten file_collections; sizes appear only as rounded free text inside notes ('Size reported by the repository as 4.6 GB'). The record documents this decision in source_caveats rather than presenting conversions of rounded figures as exact, which is sound practice, but the effect is that no program can compute the release size.
recommendation: Retrieve exact byte counts from the Dataverse API (which exposes them) and populate total_bytes per collection, retaining the rounded repository figures in notes.

description: Bias documentation is narrow and no fairness analysis is present. known_biases carries two entries (selection_bias, sampling_bias) and no AIO or CROISSANT RAI term mappings. Measurement and technical bias is absent despite four measurement modalities where it dominates: antibody specificity and cross-reactivity in the IF imaging, abundance-dependent detection bias in AP-MS and SEC-MS, and variable knockdown efficiency in CRISPRi. The record's own known_limitations notes that the modalities 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap', a coverage bias that is not carried into known_biases.
recommendation: Add measurement_bias entries for antibody specificity, MS abundance bias and CRISPRi knockdown variability; map each bias to an AIO term; and add a fairness or coverage analysis quantifying per-modality protein overlap.

description: The keyword 'mass spectroscopy' is an incorrect term for the methods used. The dataset employs mass spectrometry (AP-MS, SEC-MS), which the record names correctly everywhere else; 'spectroscopy' denotes a different class of technique and will match the wrong queries.
recommendation: Replace the keyword 'mass spectroscopy' with 'mass spectrometry'.

description: Several creator names are retained in surname-initial form rather than full personal names ('Axelsson U', 'Gao J', 'Lee YH', 'Sigaeva A', 'Ballllosero Navarro F'), and 'Ballllosero' contains a probable orthographic error (four consecutive 'l' characters). Most of these entries nonetheless carry ORCID iDs, which disambiguate them.
recommendation: Expand surname-initial forms to full names by resolving the attached ORCID records, and correct the 'Ballllosero' spelling.

description: publisher is given only as the opaque CURIE 'ROR:0153tk833' with no human-readable label. The identifier resolves to the University of Virginia and is consistent with the DOI prefix and landing-page domain, so this is a readability rather than an accuracy defect.
recommendation: Carry both the ROR identifier and the organization name.

description: Two disclosed source discrepancies remain unresolved in the record: the project end date (NIH RePORTER 2026-08-31 versus the Dataverse maintenance statement 'end of the project in November 2026'), and the affiliation of Andrej Sali (UCSD per the Dataverse release, UCSF per the Nature publication and preprint). In both cases the record states the conflict, names the competing sources and explains its resolution rule rather than silently picking one.
recommendation: No correction required; the disclosure is the correct handling. Resolve upstream with the project if a single authoritative value becomes available.

description: The citation string cites this release as 'V2' while the version field records '2.0'. Minor, but it compounds the version-sequence issue above for anyone matching a citation to a deposit version.
recommendation: Align the version token in the citation with the value of the version field.

description: regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level is 'unrestricted', but the same record documents a commercial-use prohibition (data_use_permission: no_commercial_use), a ShareAlike obligation, a Data Access Committee supervising dual licensing, and two external perturb-seq resources 'listed as embargoed'. 'Unrestricted' is defensible for access confidentiality (data_governance.access_review_process states 'no access request is required for the published files'), but the single-token label under-states the documented use restrictions and the partial embargo.
recommendation: Qualify the confidentiality classification, e.g. 'unrestricted access, restricted reuse (non-commercial, ShareAlike)', or add a note distinguishing access confidentiality from use restriction so the enum value is not read as unrestricted reuse.

description: Version-number inversion across the release series: the current June 2026 release carries version '2.0', while version_access lists the superseded 'October 2025 Data Release (Beta), Version 2.1' and 'June 2025 Data Release (Beta), Version 2.1'. A later release bearing a lower version string is confusing on its face.
recommendation: The record does explain the mechanism (each quarterly release is a separate Dataverse dataset with its own internal version history); state that explanation adjacent to the `version` field itself, or adopt a release-scoped version label such as '2026-06 (Dataverse V2)'.

description: Creator affiliations are recorded in the structured `affiliations` field for only 5 of 47 creators (the five ROR:0153tk833 University of Virginia authors). The remaining 42 affiliations exist only as free text inside `notes` (e.g. 'Ideker T, University of California San Diego'), so they are human-readable but not machine-resolvable, and no ROR identifiers are asserted for them.
recommendation: Promote the affiliation names now held in `notes` into structured `affiliations` entries with ROR identifiers (e.g. ROR:0168r3w48 for UCSD, ROR:043mz5j54 for UCSF, ROR:00f54p054 for Stanford), retaining `notes` only for genuinely unstructurable remarks.

description: Software tools are named with resolvable URLs but never with version numbers: node2vec, the Cell Mapping Toolkit (github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline), FAIRSCAPE, the Integrative Modeling Platform, the Human Protein Atlas deep learning model and the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit all appear without a release, tag or commit. version_access asserts that 'Software packages used to produce each release are versioned, and the version used to produce a dataset is referenced in that dataset's metadata' — a pointer to versions held elsewhere rather than the versions themselves.
recommendation: Record the pinned version or commit for each named tool in the datasheet itself, so that the reuse claim is checkable without resolving the RO-Crate metadata.

description: The most detailed processing documentation describes a pipeline whose outputs are excluded from this release. All four preprocessing_strategies entries (node2vec PPI embedding, HPA image embedding, contrastive co-embedding, community detection) and the labeling_strategies entry carry source_caveats stating these are MuSIC pipeline steps and that 'the June 2026 release states that computed cell maps are not included in this release'. The processing actually applied to the distributed artifacts is therefore covered only by RO-Crate packaging and a general QC statement.
recommendation: Add a short strategy entry describing the preprocessing actually applied to the released archives per modality (e.g. MS search engine and FDR thresholds for SEC-MS/AP-MS, image acquisition/QC for IF, guide assignment and cell filtering for perturb-seq), separate from the MuSIC-pipeline description. The existing caveats are exemplary and should be kept.

description: No consent or ethical-sourcing provenance is documented for the donor material underlying the two cell lines, although donor-level descriptors are disclosed: MDA-MB-468 'established from a metastatic site pleural effusion of a 51-year-old black female with a metastatic mammary adenocarcinoma' and KOLF2.1J 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor'. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and no informed_consent field is present. The 'no human subjects' determination is correct for secondary use of established lines, but the consent basis of the source material is asserted only indirectly ('the project describes these lines as ethically sourced').
recommendation: Cite the donor consent provenance for each line (ATCC's terms for MDA-MB-468; the HipSci/KOLF2.1J broad-consent documentation) so that the ethical-sourcing claim is traceable rather than asserted.

description: Governance and privacy content is present in prose but absent from the designated structured fields. The Data Governance Committee contact (Jillian Parker, jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu) is stated inside regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance rather than in regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact; reidentification risk is argued in prose ('cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject') with no participant_privacy.reidentification_risk field; and there is no data_protection_impacts field.
recommendation: Move the governance contact into governance_committee_contact and record the reidentification-risk determination in its own field, so machine consumers of the ethics block do not have to parse narrative text.

description: File sizes are given only in free text inside file_collections descriptions ('untreated (4.6 GB), paclitaxel-treated (3.8 GB) and vorinostat-treated (4.2 GB)', '113.3 KB', '171.8 KB', '1.1 MB'). The structured total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes fields are unpopulated, so no machine-readable size is available despite the information being known.
recommendation: Populate total_bytes per collection and total_size_bytes for the release; the values are already known to the author and are printed by Dataverse.

description: `publisher` is omitted with the explanation 'The bundle names no publisher for the release', yet the record's own `citation` ends 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C, University of Virginia Dataverse, V2', and maintainers name 'University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData)' as archival steward. The publishing organization is therefore stated twice in the record while the dedicated field is left empty.
recommendation: Set publisher to the University of Virginia Dataverse (LibraData), which the citation already identifies; the conservative omission is stricter than the record's own evidence requires.

description: The keyword 'mass spectroscopy' is a terminological error for mass spectrometry, the technique actually used throughout (SEC-MS, AP-MS). Spectroscopy and spectrometry are distinct methods, so the keyword misdescribes the assay and will not match controlled-vocabulary searches.
recommendation: Replace 'mass spectroscopy' with 'mass spectrometry'. (If the term was transcribed verbatim from the upstream Dataverse keyword list, keep the transcription but add the corrected term alongside it.)

description: Bias documentation covers representation and selection bias but not measurement or technical bias, which are material for these modalities: antibody specificity and cross-reactivity in the Human Protein Atlas IF panel, abundance-dependent detection bias in SEC-MS/AP-MS, and guide-RNA efficiency variance in the CRISPRi screens. Only one of the two documented biases (selection_bias) carries a mitigation_strategy. No AIO or CROISSANT RAI ontology term identifiers accompany the bias_type values.
recommendation: Add measurement_bias entries for the antibody, mass-spectrometry and guide-efficiency effects, attach a mitigation or explicit non-mitigability statement to representation_bias, and map each bias_type to its AIO/CROISSANT RAI term identifier.

description: The `notes` field mixes release-scope and project-scope quantities: 1,374 protein interactions, 53,788 immunofluorescent images, 7,023 proteins and 21.4 TB are project-wide portal totals, while 11,739 genes appears at both scopes. This is not an internal contradiction — the record itself states 'the portal total and the atlas figure coincide but are stated at different scopes' — but the figures sit in a field a reader may take as describing this release.
recommendation: No correction needed to the facts; consider separating project-wide totals into a clearly labelled subfield so they cannot be mistaken for release-scope counts. Recorded here as a handled ambiguity rather than an error.

description: Stated archive sizes are implausibly small for the described content and this is not flagged anywhere in the record. The KOLF2.1J CRISPRi perturbation cell atlas archive is given as 30.2 KB and the accompanying raw sequence archive as 73.3 KB, yet the same record describes a genome-scale screen covering 11,739 targeted genes; the SEC-MS archives are 171.8 KB and 93.9 KB and the AP-MS archives 113.3 KB and 135.8 KB. Only the three immunofluorescence archives (3.8-4.6 GB) are of an order consistent with their described contents. Either the small archives are pointers/manifests rather than data, or the sizes are transcribed incorrectly; the record asserts neither.
recommendation: State for each small archive whether it contains data or only manifests/pointers to externally deposited data (MassIVE, Figshare, SRA), and record machine-readable total_bytes per resource so the size/content mismatch can be checked rather than inferred.

description: distribution_formats declares a single format, ZIP (application/zip), for all ten deliverables, so the formats a reuser actually parses — image formats for 53,788 immunofluorescence images, matrix/count formats for perturb-seq, mass-spectrometry table formats for SEC-MS and AP-MS — are nowhere stated. The record simultaneously claims RO-Crate packaging, conformance to https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema and AI-ready status, which cannot be assessed at the level of an opaque container.
recommendation: Enumerate the internal file formats and media types within each ZIP archive (e.g., OME-TIFF/PNG, MTX/H5AD, mzML/TSV) alongside the container format.

description: conforms_to asserts 'RO-Crate packaging with provenance graphs and rich metadata, produced using the FAIRSCAPE framework', but no RO-Crate or provenance artifact is identifiable among the ten enumerated resources. The only candidate is cm4ai_release_metadata.zip (1.1 MB), whose description is simply 'One ZIP archive (1.1 MB) of release metadata' and which is not stated to contain the RO-Crate or the provenance graph.
recommendation: State explicitly which archive carries the RO-Crate metadata descriptor and provenance graph, and describe the graph's serialization so the PROV claim is verifiable.

description: The provenance and derivation claims rest on an acknowledged inference rather than documentation. preprocessing_strategies and the derived acquisition_method both carry source_caveats stating that the atlas-from-raw derivation is 'Inferred from the paired archive names cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_cell_atlas.zip and cm4ai_perturb-seq_KOLF2_raw_sra.zip' because 'the June 2026 release listing carries no per-file processing description'. The structured provenance fields was_derived_from and parent_datasets are unpopulated.
recommendation: Populate was_derived_from linking each processed archive to its raw source, and document the actual processing pipeline (alignment, guide assignment, QC thresholds) rather than inferring derivation from filenames.

description: Temporal ordering inside the release is internally inconsistent: version 2.0 is issued 2026-06-17 while three immunofluorescence archives carry issued dates of 2026-07-15, a month after the version they belong to was published. The record discloses this in source_caveats but does not resolve it into a version.
recommendation: Either assign the later-published image archives to a distinct Dataverse version or state that version 2.0 was amended on 2026-07-15.

description: The description text is flagged by the record itself as possibly carried forward from prior releases: the Dataverse description block 'ends with a trailing (2025-06-30) stamp identical to that on the June 2025 and October 2025 releases'. The June 2026 file listing also carries no per-file descriptions, so modality and content detail for individual archives is imported from the preprint and earlier release pages. Content statements about this release therefore have weaker evidentiary standing than their confident phrasing suggests, even though the record flags each instance.
recommendation: Obtain release-specific per-file descriptions from the depositor so that modality, protein counts and staining details are asserted for this release rather than inherited.

description: A grant_number slot is used for a non-identifier: funders[University of Virginia].grants[0].grant_number is 'Frederick Thomas Fund', with the note conceding 'no numeric identifier is given'. The two NIH values (1OT2OD032742-01, 5U54HG012513-02) are well-formed NIH award numbers; the third breaks the field's type expectation.
recommendation: Record 'Frederick Thomas Fund' as a fund/award name rather than a grant_number, leaving the identifier slot empty.

description: Donor-origin consent provenance is absent while human-derived material is central. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false — a self-consistent pair for cell-line work — but both source lines derive from identified human donors (MDA-MB-468 from a 51-year-old Black female; KOLF2.1J from a healthy male Northern European donor) and no consent or provenance-of-consent statement accompanies either.
recommendation: Add the donor-consent provenance for both cell lines (ATCC terms; HipSci consent framework and MTA) to close the gap between 'de-identified samples' and the human origin of the material.

description: Ethical review contact identity is asserted across mismatched affiliations: Vardit Ravitsky is given ORCID 0000-0002-7080-8801 with affiliation University of Montreal but an email at thehastingscenter.org. The record flags the mismatch and explains the identification, so this is a disclosed uncertainty rather than an error.
recommendation: Confirm the current affiliation of the ethics contact so the ORCID, institution and contact domain agree.

description: Version numbering across the release series is non-monotonic as presented: this June 2026 release is Dataverse version 2.0 while the earlier October 2025 and June 2025 releases are listed at Dataverse version 2.1. This is coherent because each release is a separate DOI versioned independently, but it is not stated and reads as a regression.
recommendation: Note explicitly that Dataverse version numbers are per-DOI and do not order the release series; the release date and DOI do.

description: Access status is stated two ways without reconciliation: data_governance notes 'All ten archives in this release are listed with public file access', while confidential_elements records that external data links for perturb-seq in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and in MDA-MB-468 cells are 'marked embargoed'. The two are reconcilable (deposited archives public, external links embargoed) but the record does not say so.
recommendation: State that the embargo applies to externally linked components only, and give the expected embargo lift conditions or dates.

description: The 21.4 TB, 53,788 image and 1,374 interaction figures in notes are read by the record as cumulative project-wide holdings, an inference it flags; they sit beside enumerated archive sizes totalling roughly 12.6 GB for this release. A reader taking the notes figures as release-scoped would overstate the release by three orders of magnitude.
recommendation: Label the portal Data Insights figures explicitly as cumulative project totals wherever they appear, and give a release-scoped total size in bytes.

description: Version numbering regresses across releases: this June 2026 release declares version: '2.0', while version_access records the earlier October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) and June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) as 'version 2.1'. A successor release carrying a lower version string than its predecessors is not explained anywhere in the record, and source_caveats does not flag it among the source conflicts it does disclose.
recommendation: State the versioning scheme explicitly (e.g. Dataverse major version V2 vs. internal release version) or correct the version string so that release order and version order agree; if the source itself is inconsistent, record it in source_caveats alongside the other disclosed conflicts.

description: The single erratum is self-referential and internally contradictory: 'The June 2025 Data Release was published as a revision of the preceding June 2025 release'. From related_datasets, the June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R, published 2025-07-01) succeeded the March 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/B35XWX, published 2025-03-03), so 'preceding June 2025' should read 'preceding March 2025'. The erratum_url does resolve to the correct release DOI, and the described changes (RGB images, RO-Crate metadata corrections, naming conventions) match the June 2025 entry in related_datasets.
recommendation: Correct the erratum text to name the March 2025 release as the revised predecessor.

description: confidential_elements declares confidential_elements_present: true with a named pre-publication embargo on perturb-seq data, and third_party_sharing repeats that the perturb-seq deposits are embargoed, yet regulatory_restrictions carries only other_compliance and no confidentiality_level classification. A record that asserts confidential content should classify its confidentiality level.
recommendation: Populate regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level with the applicable ConfidentialityLevelEnum value and state the embargo end date or release condition for the perturb-seq components.

description: No data-preparation documentation for the released files: preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols and missing_data_documentation are all absent. The MuSIC pipeline described in notes is explicitly scoped out ('Computed cell maps are not included in this release, so those pipeline stages describe project tooling and planned future releases rather than processing applied to the data released here'), so a reuser cannot tell how, for example, the perturb-seq cell atlas archive was derived from raw sequence.
recommendation: Document the processing actually applied to each released collection (alignment/quantification for perturb-seq, search engine and FDR settings for SEC-MS and AP-MS, image processing for the IF archives) with tool names, versions and URLs.

description: collection_timeframes is absent. acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms and data_collectors are all well populated, but no acquisition window is given for any modality; created_on (2025-02-27) and issued (2026-06-17) are record and publication dates, not collection dates.
recommendation: Add collection_timeframes with per-modality acquisition date ranges, or state explicitly that the sources do not report them.

description: future_use_impacts is absent, so the record offers no social-impact analysis or mitigation strategies even though it carries prohibited_uses, discouraged_uses and a representation_bias entry that would anchor one. This caps both Q18 and Q20.
recommendation: Add future_use_impacts describing foreseeable downstream risks (e.g. over-generalisation from two cell lines to population-level biology) with stated mitigations.

description: Provenance is expressed only in prose and typed dataset relationships: was_derived_from, parent_datasets and missing_data_documentation are all absent. Agents (Lundberg Lab, Krogan Lab), activities (AP-MS, SEC-MS, ICC-IF, perturb-seq) and entities (ten enumerated files) are each documented, but no field links a given activity and agent to a given output file, so the entity-activity-agent chain must be inferred by the reader.
recommendation: Add was_derived_from per file collection linking source cell line, acquisition activity and performing laboratory, exploiting the RO-Crate conformance already declared.

description: distribution_formats declares a single container format (ZIP, application/zip) for all ten files and no internal format is named anywhere, so the actual data encodings (e.g. mzML/raw for mass spectrometry, matrix or h5 for perturb-seq, TIFF/PNG for the image archives) are undeclared. The record is genuinely multi-modal in content, but its declared format variety is one, which limits machine-actionable interoperability and forces a download to discover what the archives contain.
recommendation: Declare the internal file formats and media types per collection in addition to the ZIP container.

description: Temporal oddity, disclosed but not reconciled: the dataset issued date is 2026-06-17, while the three immunofluorescence archives carry issued: 2026-07-15, i.e. component files post-date the release they belong to by four weeks. distribution_dates records the same split, so this appears to be faithful reporting of a staged publication rather than an error, but the record does not say so.
recommendation: State that the image archives were added to the release after its initial publication date.

description: Two quantitative source conflicts are carried unresolved, though both are explicitly disclosed and neither is silently adjusted: total_size_bytes (12.6 GB, this record's own computation) versus the project portal's 21.4 TB 'Data volume', and 563 versus 464 immunofluorescence proteins of interest across prior releases. source_caveats states the tier ranking used and marks the superseded reading.
recommendation: No change required to the disclosure practice; if possible confirm the release-level volume with the repository to retire the 21.4 TB comparison.

description: ethical_reviews documents two named project ethics leads with ORCIDs and e-mail addresses but records no IRB or ethics-board determination, protocol number, or exemption finding. This is coherent with human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects: false and with the laboratory cell-line provenance, so it is noted rather than penalised, and Q8 is not scored under the human-subjects gate.
recommendation: If a formal non-human-subjects determination exists, record its identifier; otherwise state that no IRB review was required and why.

description: Keyword 'mass spectroscopy' is the wrong term for the technique the record describes throughout (mass spectrometry, in AP-MS and SEC-MS). Discoverability is only mildly affected because 'AP-MS' and 'SEC-MS' are also present as keywords.
recommendation: Replace 'mass spectroscopy' with 'mass spectrometry'.

description: Three Q1 mandatory-field slots are unpopulated: variables (no variable-level metadata for any modality), parent_datasets (prior releases are instead expressed as related_datasets with is_new_version_of), and regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level. A top-level resources list is also absent, though per-file resources are fully enumerated inside file_collections.
recommendation: Add variables (or a per-collection data dictionary reference) and mirror the version lineage into parent_datasets.

description: Version number regresses relative to its own declared predecessors. This record declares version '2.0' for the June 2026 release, while version_access records the June 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/F3TD5R) and the October 2025 release (doi:10.18130/V3/K7TGEM) as 'Version 2.1'. A later release carrying a lower version string than the two releases it supersedes cannot be ordered by version alone, which undermines the version_access chain it is meant to anchor.
recommendation: Reconcile the release-level version string with the Dataverse version numbers of the prior releases, or state explicitly in version_access that Dataverse version numbers are per-deposit and are not a monotonic sequence across the CM4AI release series.

description: Temporal ordering of the declared dates is internally inconsistent and the record says so itself. created_on is 2025-02-27 and issued is 2026-06-17, a sixteen-month gap; source_caveats states the Data Creation Date is 'reused verbatim from earlier releases in this Dataverse collection' and that the release page carries a Dataset Description block dated 2025-06-30 although the release was published 2026-06-17. last_updated_on (2026-07-15) correctly follows the immunofluorescence file publication date, so the collection-to-publication ordering is not violated, but created_on does not describe this release's data.
recommendation: Either record a creation date specific to this release's data generation or move the inherited 2025-02-27 deposit date to maintainers/distribution_dates where it is described as a deposit date rather than a creation date.

description: conforms_to asserts RO-Crate packaging while simultaneously disclaiming the evidence for it: the value states that 'the June 2026 release page does not itself restate the packaging format, and its file listing names only cm4ai_release_metadata.zip without stating its internal format.' conforms_to_standard nonetheless asserts RO_CRATE as an unqualified enum value, so a machine reader receives a firm standards claim that the free-text qualifies away.
recommendation: Qualify or drop the conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE assertion for this release until the packaging of cm4ai_release_metadata.zip is confirmed, so that the structured claim and the narrative caveat agree.

description: Bias taxonomy under-covers a bias the record documents elsewhere. known_biases lists a single entry, representation_bias. sampling_strategies independently records is_random: false, is_representative: false and 'Targeted selection of cell lines and perturbation targets rather than random sampling', and known_limitations records that the three assays 'interrogate sets of proteins which incompletely overlap'. Both are selection/coverage biases with direct consequences for models trained on the release, and neither is categorized in known_biases.
recommendation: Add known_biases entries of type selection_bias for the targeted (non-random) choice of cell lines and perturbation targets, and for the incomplete protein-set overlap across SEC-MS, IF imaging and perturb-seq modalities.

description: External repository deposits are named without accession identifiers. raw_data_sources and third_party_sharing state that SEC-MS and AP-MS data are 'Available at the MassIVE Repository' and the CRISPRi atlas is 'Available at Figshare', but give no MassIVE MSV number, no ProteomeXchange PXD number and no Figshare DOI. The contrast is visible inside the record: the related_datasets entry for the separate U2OS Nature paper does supply MSV000097168 and PXD052362.
recommendation: Add the MassIVE/ProteomeXchange accessions and the Figshare DOI for this release's own deposits so the third-party copies are resolvable rather than merely named.

description: Embargoed content is declared but no access path is given for it. known_limitations and raw_data_sources state that perturb-seq data in KOLF2.1J iPSCs and in MDA-MB-468 cells are 'Embargoed', yet no embargo end date, request procedure or Data Access Committee route for embargoed material is documented, even though data_governance describes an access_review_process for commercial dual licensing.
recommendation: State the embargo expiry date and the request procedure for embargoed subsets, linking them to the Data Access Committee contact already recorded.

description: Human-subject negation is well argued but the donor consent chain is not documented. human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects is false and is_deidentified explains that tissue-culture data 'cannot be matched, with current knowledge, to a human subject' — a defensible position. However direct_collection records that KOLF2.1J was 'derived from a healthy male Northern European donor' via HipSci, so human-derived material with a named donor phenotype is in scope and no consent or provenance-of-consent statement accompanies it.
recommendation: Add a short statement of the consent and ethical-sourcing basis for the KOLF2.1J and MDA-MB-468 lines (HipSci/ATCC terms) to close the donor-provenance gap without contradicting the not-human-subjects determination.

description: File sizes are present only as free text inside file_collections.notes ('113.3 KB', '3.8 GB', '4.6 GB', ...). total_size_bytes is absent and no file_collections.total_bytes is populated, so no size is machine-readable despite the record enumerating all ten archives with checksums.
recommendation: Populate file_collections.total_bytes per archive and a release-level total_size_bytes, retaining the human-readable sizes in notes.

description: Access URL is a non-resolvable API stem. distribution_formats.access_urls gives only 'https://dataverse.lib.virginia.edu/api/access/datafile/' with no file identifiers appended, and no download_url is recorded, so the documented access path stops one step short of retrieval for each of the ten archives.
recommendation: Record per-file Dataverse datafile identifiers or persistent file DOIs, or add the dataset landing page on dataverse.lib.virginia.edu as the canonical download entry point.

description: Governance is documented but the confidentiality classification is absent. regulatory_restrictions contains only a free-text statement that FDA regulation does not apply; regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level, hipaa_compliant and other_compliance are unpopulated, and no data_protection_impacts assessment is recorded, even though a Data Access Committee and named governance contact exist.
recommendation: Set an explicit confidentiality_level (public/open, given CC BY-NC-SA distribution) and state that HIPAA does not apply, rather than leaving the classification unstated.

description: Creator identifiers mix resolvable ORCIDs with locally minted, non-resolvable person IDs. Eight creators (Axelsson U, Chinn B, Fall J, Johannesson A, Khaliq H, Muralidharan M, Pan E, Polacco B, Zhang Y) carry identifiers of the form doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#person-<surname>-<initial>, which are fragment identifiers on the dataset DOI and do not resolve to a person record. Names for these creators are surname-plus-initial only, which source_caveats acknowledges.
recommendation: Supply ORCIDs where they exist, or omit the identifier rather than minting a dataset-DOI fragment that a consumer may mistake for a resolvable person PID.

description: Distribution format variety is nominally one (ZIP) because ZIP is a container, not a data format. The record enumerates ten archives with checksums, sizes and publication dates but never states the internal formats (image format for the 12.6 GB of confocal IF data, matrix/h5ad format for perturb-seq, tabular format for SEC-MS and AP-MS elution and interaction data), so a reuser cannot determine what they will find inside before download.
recommendation: Add distribution_formats entries for the internal formats of each archive (e.g. OME-TIFF/PNG for IF images, TSV/CSV for MS tables, MTX/H5AD for perturb-seq matrices) alongside the ZIP container.

description: Processing documentation is absent for the released data. None of preprocessing_strategies, cleaning_strategies, labeling_strategies, machine_annotation_tools, annotation_analyses, imputation_protocols or missing_data_documentation is populated, even though seven of the ten archives are labelled collection_type: processed_data. The MuSIC pipeline and Cell Mapping Toolkit are described in notes and external_resources, but those produce the computed cell maps that this release explicitly excludes, so they do not document how the released processed files were derived from the raw acquisitions.
recommendation: Document the per-modality processing that turned raw acquisitions into the processed_data archives (peptide search engine and database for MS, elution-profile scoring, guide calling and QC filters for perturb-seq, image QC/segmentation for IF), with tool names and versions.

description: collection_timeframes asserts a single unanchored figure ('The data were collected over a period of 12 months') while its own source_caveats records a four-year IRB study with pilot collection begun November 2023 and still ongoing November 2024, plus a feasibility window of 5 June to 28 July 2023. No start or end date is given for the released dataset's collection window, so a reuser cannot situate the data in time. The conflict is disclosed rather than concealed, but it remains unresolved.
recommendation: Record explicit start and end dates for the version 3.1.0 collection window, and state whether the 12-month figure is a subset of the wider four-year study period.  This reduced Q12 from 5 to 4, since 'timeframes' is one of the three named components of the 5 band.

description: The structured flag is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present is false, yet participant_privacy.reidentification_risk states that k-anonymization with k of 2 or more is not achieved and that re-identification by voice cannot be entirely excluded. The registered-access release ships spectrograms, Mel spectrograms and MFCCs, which are speaker-discriminative representations of the excluded waveform; the boolean therefore under-represents the residual risk the prose itself describes.
recommendation: Qualify identifiable_elements_present, or state explicitly that the flag refers to direct and HIPAA Safe Harbor identifiers only and that voice-derived features retain residual speaker-discriminative signal mitigated by the registered-access tier. Did not reduce Q8: the prose discloses the residual risk and the two-tier access model is a proportionate control, so ethics coverage remains comprehensive.

description: The description reports a consortium self-assessment of 100 percent on provenance ('transparent, traceable, interpretable, key actors identified') and 100 percent on FAIRness, while known_limitations records that the same self-assessment fails the data quality criterion under characterization and the domain-appropriate and associated criteria under sustainability. The record carries no was_derived_from or parent_datasets linkage, so the 100 percent provenance claim is not machine-evidenced within the datasheet itself.
recommendation: Attribute the AI-readiness percentages explicitly as consortium self-assessment (already partly done) and add was_derived_from / parent_datasets linkages so the provenance claim is evidenced by structured fields rather than prose alone.

description: The description enumerates five disease cohort categories including 'pediatric voice and speech disorders', but the record's scope is the adult dataset: human_subject_research.special_populations and related_datasets state that pediatric participants were released as a separate Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset. subpopulations repeats the five-category list and then notes 'the adult dataset contains adult participants only'. A reader skimming the description could infer pediatric data is included in this release.
recommendation: State in the description that the pediatric cohort is documented only as context and is distributed as the separate related dataset doi:10.13026/h995-bt35.

description: RRID:SCR_007345 appears inside the dataset citation string. The format is a valid RRID (RRID:SCR_XXXXX), but SCR_007345 identifies the PhysioNet resource, not this dataset; no dataset-level RRID is asserted and the record has no top-level rrid field.
recommendation: Clarify in the citation or a dedicated field that the RRID identifies the hosting repository, or add a dataset-level RRID if one has been minted.

description: Grant identifier renderings vary across the cited sources (OT2OD032720, 3OT2OD032720-01S1, 3OT2OD032720-01S3, 1OT2OD032720-01, and the malformed '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' in a documentation footer). The two carried in funders.grants are both well-formed NIH identifiers and the variance is disclosed in source_caveats, but the malformed footer variant is quoted without being marked as a transcription error.
recommendation: Mark '3Tf-OTOD03272001S2' explicitly as an apparent typographic corruption of 3OT2OD032720-01S2 in the upstream source.

description: Only four keywords are supplied (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) for a dataset spanning five clinical cohorts and dozens of conditions. No disease terms, modality terms (spectrogram, MFCC, cough, respiratory), standard ontology codes (SNOMED CT, ICD-10) or method terms appear in keywords, even though labeling_strategies states labels follow ICD-10 codes and instances carry B2AI_TOPIC / B2AI_SUBSTRATE ontology terms.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least eight, drawing on the cohort names, acoustic modalities and the ICD-10 / B2AI ontology terms already used elsewhere in the record. This is the binding constraint on Q3.

description: Structural containment fields resources and parent_datasets are absent, and variables enumerates only four columns (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames) for a release that includes phenotype tables covering confounders, demographics, diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaires and task metadata. No total_size_bytes, file_collections or total_file_count is given; per-feature file counts appear only inside source_caveats prose.
recommendation: Add file_collections with byte totals and file counts, and extend variables to cover the principal phenotype table columns or reference the published JSON data dictionaries per table. This is the binding constraint on Q1.

description: Tool documentation names the software used (sparc, openSMILE, Parselmouth, Praat, ppgs, Whisper Large, b2aiprep, senselab) with signal-processing parameters, but supplies no version numbers for any of them; 'Whisper Large' names a model size, not a pinned revision. tool_accuracy states transcriptions came from off-the-shelf models 'not audited for correctness', so no annotation quality metric is available. imputation_protocols is absent, though handling_strategy states no imputation is applied.
recommendation: Pin version numbers or commit hashes for each preprocessing tool and add repository URLs alongside each named tool. This reduced Q11 from 5 to 4.

description: Demographic sub-populations are named by axis (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and their skew is described qualitatively, but no counts or distributions per stratum are given, and the inclusion and exclusion criteria are referred to ('the corresponding inclusion and exclusion criteria') without being enumerated. Only English-only and adult-only exclusions are stated concretely, via known_limitations.
recommendation: Publish per-stratum counts for the demographic axes and enumerate the per-cohort inclusion and exclusion criteria. This reduced Q15 from 5 to 4.

description: known_biases uses four taxonomy-conformant bias_type values with clear descriptions, but only one of the four carries a mitigation_strategy and only one carries affected_subsets. No quantitative fairness analysis (subgroup counts, parity metrics) and no explicit AIO ontology mappings are present; fairness is treated qualitatively via future_use_impacts and discouraged_uses.
recommendation: Add mitigation_strategy and affected_subsets to each documented bias and attach AIO identifiers to the bias_type values; supply subgroup distribution tables to support quantitative fairness assessment. This reduced Q20 from 5 to 4.

description: Identifier rendering is inconsistent: doi is the bare string '10.13026/8xbn-nq66' while id and version_access.latest_version_doi and related_datasets.target_dataset use the 'doi:' CURIE prefix. There is no top-level publisher field, although PhysioNet is identified as host in citation, maintainers and data_governance.stewardship_roles.
recommendation: Normalize DOI rendering across fields and add an explicit publisher field naming PhysioNet (MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology).

description: Temporal inconsistency in the collection window. collection_timeframes states the data were collected 'over a period of twelve months' (and known_limitations repeats 'approximately twelve months'), but the same field records accrual across releases published November 2024 (306 participants), version 2.0 April 2025 (+136) and version 3.0.0 December 2025 (+391), a span of roughly twenty-five months of accrual. No absolute collection start or end date is given anywhere in the record, so the twelve-month figure cannot be reconciled with the release timeline.
recommendation: Record absolute collection start and end dates, and state whether the twelve-month figure describes a single site's enrollment window, the first release's collection period, or per-participant follow-up, rather than the full multi-site accrual.

description: data_protection_impacts states plainly that 'No analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects has been conducted', while the same record documents biometric voice data, psychiatric and cognitive-impairment cohorts, an explicit statement that k-anonymity with k>=2 is not achieved, and an acknowledgement that voice can never be fully de-identified. The absence of a formal DPIA is honestly disclosed and partly offset by ethicist review of sensitive fields and the published memorandum 'Ethical Justification for Controlled Access to Raw Voice Data Samples', but the substantive gap remains for a dataset of this sensitivity.
recommendation: Conduct and document a formal data protection impact assessment covering the residual re-identification risk of derived acoustic features, and link it from data_protection_impacts alongside the existing ethical-justification memorandum.

description: The final errata entry asserts 'No formal erratum is published', directly following three concrete erratum entries describing spectrogram reprocessing in v2.0.0, an authorship correction in v2.0.1 and Parquet repairs plus diagnosis back-fill in v3.1.0. The intended meaning is presumably that no standalone erratum document exists and corrections are carried in the changelog, but as written the list contradicts itself.
recommendation: Rephrase the final entry as a note on erratum publication practice (for example, 'corrections are published in the per-version changelog rather than as standalone errata') instead of as an erratum that denies the preceding three.

description: The standards-conformance claims do not cover the artifacts actually released. conforms_to states BIDS v1.9.0 applies to 'the audio dataset layout and the phenotype folder organization rather than to the Parquet feature files of the published feature-only release' — that is, not to the dense features that constitute the release — while conforms_to_schema points to the LinkML data-sheets schema, which governs this datasheet rather than the data files. Column-level structure for the released files rests on the per-file JSON data dictionaries, which are documented but are not a registered standard.
recommendation: State explicitly which schema or specification governs the Parquet feature tables and their column semantics, and consider registering the JSON data dictionaries against a named standard so conformance claims attach to the released artifacts.

description: regulatory_restrictions.regulatory_restrictions asserts that 'No export controls or other regulatory restrictions apply to the dataset or to individual instances', while regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance in the same block documents a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas, and hipaa_compliant is set to 'compliant'. The two senses (trade/export control versus privacy regulation) are distinguishable, but the blanket phrase 'or other regulatory restrictions' overreaches.
recommendation: Narrow the assertion to export controls specifically, so it does not appear to negate the HIPAA and Certificate of Confidentiality obligations recorded immediately below it.

description: Discovery metadata is thin relative to the record's own content. keywords holds only four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) for a dataset the description characterizes as spanning five disease cohorts (voice, neurological and neurodegenerative, mood and psychiatric, respiratory, controls) and that notes 22 acoustic tasks. None of the cohort names, modality terms (spectrogram, MFCC, articulatory, cough, respiration) or coding systems referenced elsewhere (ICD-10, B2AI_TOPIC, B2AI_SUBSTRATE) appear as keywords.
recommendation: Extend keywords to at least eight terms drawn from the cohorts, acoustic modalities and feature families already enumerated in description, subpopulations and variables.

description: Two hierarchical schema fields named by Q1 are unpopulated: resources and parent_datasets. The underlying information is present in other fields — was_derived_from describes the raw audio and REDCap origin, and related_datasets carries six typed relationships with DOIs including is_new_version_of and is_version_of — so this is a placement gap rather than missing knowledge, but it reduces mandatory-field coverage to roughly 86 percent.
recommendation: Populate parent_datasets with the prior-version and source dataset DOIs already listed in related_datasets, and use resources to enumerate the feature and phenotype sub-collections described in distribution_formats.

description: Bias documentation is taxonomy-aligned but the fairness analysis is qualitative only. Two of four known_biases entries (measurement_bias, annotation_bias) carry no mitigation_strategy, and no quantitative demographic distributions, subgroup counts or fairness metrics appear anywhere: subpopulations names the demographic axes (age, gender, sex, ethnicity, socioeconomic status) and states the sample is 'skewed by site and by demographic factors' without reporting the skew. No AIO ontology term URIs are attached to the bias types.
recommendation: Add mitigation strategies for measurement_bias and annotation_bias, report per-cohort and per-demographic counts or proportions, and attach AIO/CROISSANT RAI term identifiers to each bias_type.

description: at_risk_populations.at_risk_groups_included is asserted false, yet the enrolled cohorts explicitly include participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, and a mood/psychiatric cohort encompassing schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and alcohol or substance use disorder. Under common human-subjects framings these are vulnerable populations. The record mitigates the claim by requiring capacity to consent in English, but the boolean as stated understates the population risk profile and is in tension with the subsets it describes.
recommendation: Set at_risk_groups_included to true, or narrow the claim to state that no populations requiring additional 45 CFR 46 subpart protections were enrolled, and enumerate the cognitive-impairment and psychiatric cohorts as groups receiving the documented capacity-to-consent safeguard.

description: data_protection_impacts asserts that an ethics team reviewed the data and that a controlled-access memorandum was published, while its own source_caveats records that the healthsheet answers 'No' to whether an analysis of the potential impact of the dataset and its use on data subjects was conducted. The element therefore both claims and disclaims an impact assessment.
recommendation: Distinguish the two artefacts explicitly: state that no formal DPIA was performed while a sensitive-field ethics review and a controlled-access justification memorandum were, rather than leaving the affirmative claim and the 'No' answer in the same element unreconciled.

description: The keywords field contains only four terms (voice, health, biomarkers, bridge2ai) for a dataset whose subsets enumerate more than fifty clinical conditions across four disease cohorts and whose description names seventeen acoustic tasks and thirteen validated instruments. The controlled vocabulary does not carry the topical coverage the rest of the record demonstrates, which depresses findability by topic.
recommendation: Expand keywords to at least eight terms covering the modality (speech, respiratory sounds, acoustic features), the cohorts (voice disorders, neurodegenerative, psychiatric, respiratory) and the coding systems already cited (ICD-10, BIDS).

description: Three mandatory-field slots in the Q1 list are unpopulated: resources, parent_datasets and variables. Variable-level metadata is described narratively (every table is 'paired with a JSON data dictionary keyed by column name') but no variables element is emitted, so column semantics are not machine-readable from the datasheet itself.
recommendation: Emit variables entries for at least the phenotype tables' key columns (participant_id, session_id, diagnosis, demographic fields), and express the version predecessors as parent_datasets in addition to the related_datasets typed links.

description: confidential_elements_present is false, on the stated ground that the released data contain no privileged or doctor-patient-confidential material, while regulatory_restrictions records a Certificate of Confidentiality over the identifiable source data and confidentiality_level 'restricted'. The scoping difference (released tier versus source tier) is stated elsewhere but not inside the confidential_elements element.
recommendation: Add the scope qualifier inside confidential_elements so the false value is read against the registered-access release rather than the collection as a whole.

description: Hosting and maintenance are attributed to PhysioNet / MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology in maintainers and regulatory_restrictions, while the project documentation is quoted as placing hosting with the Health Data Nexus at the University of Toronto. The record resolves the conflict in favour of the PhysioNet record and attributes the other statement to v1.0, so the residual risk to a reader is small.
recommendation: Retain the resolution as written; no change required beyond keeping the v1.0 attribution visible in the maintainers element itself.

description: No aggregate recording count and no byte sizes are recorded. instances.counts is populated for participants (833) but deliberately omitted for recordings because the preferred source gives only per-feature counts; total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent throughout, so a prospective user cannot size a download.
recommendation: Add total_size_bytes per file_collection from the PhysioNet manifest, and record the per-feature record counts as structured values rather than only in a narrative note.

description: RRID:SCR_007345 is well-formed and appears inside the citation string, but SCR_ identifiers name research resources; here it plausibly identifies the hosting repository rather than this dataset. No top-level rrid field is populated.
recommendation: State what the RRID identifies, and if a dataset-level RRID exists, record it in a dedicated rrid field rather than only inside the citation text.

description: Subpopulation distribution is qualitative only. subpopulations.distribution states that the release is not equally distributed across disease cohorts and shows skews by site and demographic factors, but no counts per cohort and no age, sex, race or ethnicity breakdown are given, despite those variables being named as the identification basis.
